title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
quote: show a 2X-3X acceleration compared to the standard T5X implementation, with identical outputs.
proves: Baseline draft-then-verify with modified rejection sampling: target distribution preserved; 2-3x on T5-XXL at batch 1. State added: a whole separate draft model plus its own KV cache; rollback = truncate both caches to the first rejected position.
does_not_prove: Says nothing about batched serving, paged KV, memory cost of the draft KV, or preemption; speedup is single-request latency.
bearing: Anchor for any idea on draft-KV memory or rollback cost; separate-draft-model state is the heaviest form.

title: SpecInfer: Accelerating Generative Large Language Model Serving with Tree-based Speculative Inference and Verification
quote: SpecInfer uses a tree topology instead of the original sequence topology to store the keys and values of all tokens
proves: Token-tree verification in one pass with a topology-aware causal mask; KV for all tree nodes stored in tree form and reused via DFS. Avg verified tokens/step (LLaMA-7B, LLaMA-68M SSM, depth 8): greedy 2.2-2.7 at width 1 to 2.9-3.9 at width 5; stochastic 1.6-1.8 to 2.2-2.4. 1.5-2.8x distributed, 2.6-3.5x offloading.
does_not_prove: Fetched text does not describe how rejected branches' KV is freed or compacted; no paged-KV or multi-tenant memory accounting.
bearing: Supports ideas about tree-shaped transient KV and its cleanup; tree width trades verify compute for acceptance.

title: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads
quote: Medusa-2 further improves the speedup to 2.3-3.6x.
proves: Extra FFN heads on the last hidden state (5 heads typical, 3-4 enough); candidates = Cartesian product of per-head top-k, 64-node sparse tree beats 256-node dense; no draft KV cache (heads are stateless, read target hidden state). 2.18x/2.83x on Vicuna-7B at batch 1. Typical acceptance is lossy (threshold).
does_not_prove: Experiments are batch 1 only; batch-size speedup deferred to TGI/TensorRT claims; KV handling of rejected tree tokens not described.
bearing: Stateless drafter: weakens ideas premised on draft-KV state; tree verification still adds transient target KV.

title: EAGLE: Speculative Sampling Requires Rethinking Feature Uncertainty
quote: EAGLE requires slightly more CUDA memory
proves: Draft = one decoder layer autoregressing on target second-to-top features plus token shifted by one; draft params 0.24B/0.37B/0.56B/0.99B for 7B/13B/33B/70B. MT-bench tau 3.62-3.98 (T=0). 2.7-3.5x latency on LLaMA2-Chat 70B; 1.97x throughput Vicuna-7B on RTX 3090 with max batch 7. State: draft KV (1 layer) + per-request last target feature.
does_not_prove: No quantified draft-KV memory; batch study tiny (max batch 7); no rollback/preemption treatment of draft KV or carried features.
bearing: Defines the EAGLE state class (draft KV + hidden features) that preemption/migration ideas would target; memory overhead claimed small.

title: EAGLE-2: Faster Inference of Language Models with Dynamic Draft Trees
quote: the confidence scores from the draft model approximate acceptance rates with small errors
proves: Dynamic draft tree chosen by draft confidence; draft is well-calibrated; 3.05x-4.26x, 20-40% over EAGLE-1.
does_not_prove: Abstract-level only; no batch-size or memory numbers fetched.
bearing: Supports confidence-driven speculation budgets (scheduling lens); calibration enables admission of draft tokens.

title: EAGLE-3: Scaling up Inference Acceleration of Large Language Models via Training-Time Test
quote: We record the low, middle, and high-level feature sequences from the target model's forward pass.
proves: Draft fuses low/mid/high target features (3k->k FC) into a single-layer decoder. MT-bench tau: EAGLE-3 6.65/6.13/5.63 vs EAGLE-2 4.83/4.05/3.67 (Vicuna13B/L3.1-8B/L3.3-70B). SGLang H100 L3.1-8B throughput gain by batch: 1.81x@2, 1.62x@8, 1.48x@16, 1.32x@32, 1.38x@64 (EAGLE-1 falls to 0.88-0.99x at 24-64). vLLM A100: EAGLE-3 1.75x@2 down to 1.01x@56, EAGLE-1 0.71x@56.
does_not_prove: No draft-KV size or memory reported; text and vLLM table disagree on peak batch; features from 3 layers must be kept per request for next draft step.
bearing: Threatens claims that spec decode is useless at batch 32-64 (still 1.3x in SGLang) but supports that the gain shrinks with batch; per-request feature state grows to 3 layers.

title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
quote: the acceptance rate of the second token prediction ranges between 85% and 90% across various generation topics
proves: MTP depth D=1, sequential modules sharing embedding and output head with main model; can be discarded or repurposed for spec decode; 2nd-token acceptance 85-90%; 1.8x TPS.
does_not_prove: Does not give MTP-module KV or memory cost at serving, nor batch-dependence of the 1.8x; depth 1 only.
bearing: MTP state is a 1-layer KV plus target hidden state, like EAGLE; weak per-request state means small rollback cost.

title: Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct (model card)
quote: Hybrid Layout: 12 * (3 * (Gated DeltaNet -> MoE) -> 1 * (Gated Attention -> MoE))
proves: Qwen3-Next ships MTP; 3 of 4 layers are Gated DeltaNet (recurrent state), so spec decode needs recurrent-state rollback; recommended vLLM config qwen3_next_mtp with num_speculative_tokens 2.
does_not_prove: No acceptance or speedup numbers; no description of how rejected tokens' DeltaNet state is restored.
bearing: Supports recurrent/SSM-state rollback as a live serving problem in production MTP models.

title: Break the Sequential Dependency of LLM Inference Using Lookahead Decoding (LMSYS blog)
quote: The 7B, 13B, and 33B models require 120x, 80x, and 56x extra FLOPs per step, respectively.
proves: Jacobi-iteration lookahead branch (2D window W,N) fills an n-gram pool; verification branch checks up to G n-grams whose first token matches; 1.5x MT-bench, >2x HumanEval, 1.8x GSM8K. State: per-request n-gram pool plus window; extra FLOPs 56-120x per step.
does_not_prove: Batch-1 numbers; huge extra FLOPs mean gains vanish once batching makes decode compute-bound; pool memory not quantified.
bearing: Threatens lookahead at serving batch sizes; n-gram pool is a cacheable/shareable state object.

title: Break the Sequential Dependency of LLM Inference Using Lookahead Decoding
quote: accelerates LLM decoding without needing auxiliary models or data stores
proves: No draft model; up to 1.8x MT-bench, 4x with strong scaling on multiple GPUs for code completion.
does_not_prove: Abstract-level only; no batch-size study fetched.
bearing: Same as A9; multi-GPU strong scaling spends spare compute that serving batches do not have.

title: prompt-lookup-decoding (GitHub repo)
quote: We modify speculative decoding where we replace the draft model with simple string matching in the prompt to generate candidate token sequences.
proves: Model-free drafter: match last n-gram in the prompt and propose its continuation; 2x-4x claimed on input-grounded tasks, ~2.4x average on summarization/context-QA; little gain on roleplay.
does_not_prove: No serving/batch results; no handling of long prompts beyond linear scan.
bearing: Prompt/n-gram drafting adds almost no state; ideas about drafter state do not apply; workload-dependence is the key variable.

title: SuffixDecoding: Extreme Speculative Decoding for Emerging AI Applications
quote: it is also straightforward to incorporate cache eviction (e.g. LRU) into Suffix Decoding
proves: Global suffix tree over past outputs + per-request tree (Ukkonen online update); memory 1,670 MB at 27M tokens to 6,150 MB at 572M tokens, linear; ~11-12 us lookup and ~4 us update per token on CPU; mean accepted tokens 6.24 (AgenticSQL) and 7.55 (SWE-Bench) vs EAGLE-3 3.16; up to 5.3x on agentic tasks; estimates ~1 month of tokens per A100 before eviction.
does_not_prove: Eviction policy not evaluated; batch/request-rate scaling not reported (bs 1, vLLM concurrency 8 or 16 inconsistent); global tree sharing across tenants, persistence, and multi-node consistency untreated.
bearing: Strong support for a caching/memory-hierarchy idea on suffix-tree eviction, persistence, and sharing; agentic repetition is the enabling workload.

title: LayerSkip: Enabling Early Exit Inference and Self-Speculative Decoding
quote: We term the union of the KV cache and the exit query as KVQ cache.
proves: Self-speculation by early exit at layer E, verify with remaining L-E layers; single KV cache shared by draft and verify plus exit-query cache; acceptance 45-99% and 1.24x-2.16x depending on task and E.
does_not_prove: Needs special training recipe; batch-1 evaluation; no rollback cost of shared KV for rejected tokens in paged serving.
bearing: Minimal extra state (one query vector per request): weakens draft-memory ideas for self-speculation.

title: SWIFT: On-the-Fly Self-Speculative Decoding for LLM Inference Acceleration
quote: SWIFT does not require auxiliary models or additional training.
proves: Plug-and-play layer-skipping drafter with on-the-fly layer selection; 1.3x-1.6x.
does_not_prove: Modest speedups at batch 1; no serving numbers; per-request skip-set adaptation state not costed.
bearing: Self-spec gains are small; layer-skip config is per-request adaptive state.

title: Draft & Verify: Lossless Large Language Model Acceleration via Self-Speculative Decoding
quote: requires no additional neural network training and no extra memory footprint.
proves: Skip intermediate layers to draft; no extra memory; up to 1.99x on LLaMA-2.
does_not_prove: Abstract only; skipped-layer KV for drafted tokens must be filled at verify; batch behavior unknown.
bearing: Zero-extra-memory baseline against which any draft-state idea must justify itself.

title: DFlash: Block Diffusion for Flash Speculative Decoding
quote: directly inject[ed] into the Key and Value projections of every draft model layer
proves: Block-diffusion drafter (5 layers default) drafts a 16-token block in one pass; target features from 5 layers projected and stored in the drafter's own KV cache across iterations. Qwen3-8B greedy tau 6.49 / 4.86x vs EAGLE-3 tau 2.96-3.40 / 1.76-2.02x. SGLang B200: 5.1x at concurrency 1 falls to 2.8x at concurrency 32; LLaMA-3.1-8B 2.4x to 1.6x; EAGLE-3 (60 tokens) below 1x at concurrency 32.
does_not_prove: No parameter count or draft-KV memory figure; block of 16 multiplies verify tokens per request; no preemption/rollback treatment of the 5-layer draft KV.
bearing: Multi-layer draft KV is a larger per-request state than EAGLE; supports memory/admission ideas, and verify-budget scheduling at high concurrency.

title: Accelerating Speculative Decoding with Block Diffusion Draft Trees
quote: The resulting tree is verified efficiently in a single target model forward pass using an ancestor-only attention mask.
proves: DDTree builds a draft tree from block-diffusion per-position distributions, verified in one pass.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no speedup numbers; serving costs of tree+block not stated.
bearing: More verify tokens per request: sharpens verification-budget scheduling questions.

title: P-EAGLE: Parallel-Drafting EAGLE with Scalable Training
quote: transforms EAGLE from autoregressive to parallel multi-token prediction via a learnable shared hidden state
proves: Parallel EAGLE drafting in vLLM; 1.10-1.36x over EAGLE-3 on GPT-OSS 120B/20B and Qwen3-Coder 30B.
does_not_prove: Abstract level; no high-concurrency or memory numbers fetched.
bearing: 2026 proposers shift drafting cost, not state; draft KV remains.

title: DSpark: Confidence-Scheduled Speculative Decoding with Semi-Autoregressive Generation
quote: indiscriminately verifying these extended blocks wastes critical batch capacity on tokens with high rejection risks
proves: Semi-AR drafter (parallel backbone + small sequential module) with per-request verification length from survival estimates and engine throughput profiles; deployed in DeepSeek-V4 serving; 60-85% faster per-user generation than MTP-1 at matched throughput.
does_not_prove: Abstract only; no detail on draft state memory or rollback; production numbers not reproducible.
bearing: Directly occupies the verification-budget scheduling space; threatens naive admission-control candidates.

title: Adaptive Verification in vLLM: DSpark confidence-scheduled verification
quote: position 5 of a confident request can outrank position 1 of a low-confidence one
proves: vLLM enable_adaptive_verification does a global top-B over survival scores across the batch; behaves like long block at low concurrency and short at high; DeepSeek-V4-Pro 8xB300, concurrency 1-256.
does_not_prove: No numeric tables in text; no draft KV/state handling discussed.
bearing: Global verify-budget allocation already in vLLM: a scheduling candidate must go beyond this.

title: EAGLE 3.1: Advancing Speculative Decoding Through Collaboration Between the EAGLE Team, vLLM, and TorchSpec
quote: EAGLE 3.1 achieves up to 2× longer acceptance length compared with EAGLE 3
proves: Adds FC normalization and post-norm hidden-state feedback; drafter attention drifts from sink tokens in long context; Kimi-K2.6 GB200 TP4: 2.03x at concurrency 1, 1.71x at 4, 1.66x at 16.
does_not_prove: No concurrency above 16; no draft-KV long-context memory numbers.
bearing: Long-context draft attention is a known weak spot; draft-KV over long contexts is open.

title: MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
quote: the draft models can occupy up to 38∼140% memory footprint of target models
proves: Self-spec with StreamingLLM draft KV (budget 512) or SnapKV (2049); critical sequence length ~4k beyond which spec decode speeds up large batches; A100 L3.1-8B StreamingLLM: 32k ctx 1.22x@32 to 1.35x@128, 8k 0.95-1.01x, 4k 0.90x@32 to 0.76x@256; up to 2.51x (SnapKV, 100k ctx, bs 41, 8xH100).
does_not_prove: Sparse-draft-KV memory not quantified; static budgets; no interaction with paged KV, prefix caching, or preemption.
bearing: Supports long-context draft-KV compression ideas; threatens short-context large-batch spec decode.

title: TriForce: Lossless Acceleration of Long Sequence Generation with Hierarchical Speculative Decoding
quote: dynamic sparse KV cache via retrieval as a draft model
proves: Hierarchical speculation: retrieval-based sparse KV of target as middle draft, tiny model on top; targets 128K contexts.
does_not_prove: Abstract only; no batch serving numbers fetched.
bearing: Prior art for draft-KV-as-subset-of-target-KV ideas.

title: TurboSpec: Closed-loop Speculation Control System for Optimizing LLM Serving Goodput
quote: speculative decoding may degrade LLM serving performance if added naively
proves: Feedback controller predicts goodput and adjusts speculation length dynamically.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not quantify high-batch degradation.
bearing: Prior art for adaptive speculation length; narrows scheduling candidates.

title: ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State
quote: The common workaround, used for example in vLLM, is to store a separate SSM state for every speculative token.
proves: vLLM keeps a full SSM state per draft token for rollback; at T=6 on Qwen3.5-122B the kernel costs 4.85x standard decoding; preallocated states cut max decode batch ~4x (window 4); vLLM spec decode falls below standard throughput at serving batch sizes; caching inputs instead gives 1.87-1.96x and 3.0-3.3x more concurrent requests.
does_not_prove: Blog, no listed authors or peer review; date inferred; no interaction with preemption, prefix caching, or migration of recurrent state.
bearing: Strong support for recurrent-state rollback as a memory/admission problem; also shows this specific gap is being closed in 2026.

title: Snakes and Ladders: Accelerating SSM Inference with Speculative Decoding
quote: they maintain a separate Markov state that makes backtracking non-trivial
proves: Two methods for SSM spec decode; 1.82x avg with n-gram drafter.
does_not_prove: Workshop abstract only; not serving-scale.
bearing: Prior art for SSM rollback.

title: Speculative Decoding (vLLM docs)
quote: Speculative decoding sampling is theoretically lossless up to the precision limits of hardware numerics.
proves: vLLM supports EAGLE, MTP, draft model, PARD, n-gram, suffix decoding, dynamic spec decode, adaptive verification, lossy FLy; aimed at medium-to-low QPS memory-bound workloads; n-gram/suffix give modest gains without extra load at peak; pipeline parallel not composable as of vllm<=0.15.0.
does_not_prove: No quantitative high-QPS data; silent on draft KV, prefix caching, hybrid models.
bearing: Shows which method states are production-relevant in the user's vLLM stack.

title: vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py
quote: Validate that all drafting layers belong to the same KVCacheGroup.
proves: vLLM drafter layers live in the target's KV cache manager as one KV cache group; rejected tokens handled by recomputing slot mapping with padding slots (no explicit free); target hidden states copied into a drafting buffer; DeepSeek V4 MTP consumes the pre-hc_head residual stream.
does_not_prove: Main-branch snapshot, not tied to vLLM 0.31.0 or vllm-metal; does not say what happens to draft KV and hidden-state buffers on preemption/swap.
bearing: Supports preemption/recovery ideas for draft KV and per-request hidden state in vLLM.

title: Unlocking Efficiency in Large Language Model Inference: A Comprehensive Survey of Speculative Decoding
quote: a comparative analysis of leading methods under third-party testing environments
proves: Survey of drafter selection and verification strategies (Spec-Bench).
does_not_prove: Pre-2024-06; no systems-state coverage.
bearing: Discovery only.

title: vLLM Ascend: Multi Token Prediction / speculative decoding guide
proves: Search snippet only: for PD-disaggregated hybrid Mamba models (Qwen-Next, Qwen3.5), num_speculative_tokens must match on P and D nodes.
does_not_prove: Not opened; implies spec-state layout leaks into KV transfer between nodes, but unconfirmed.
bearing: Possible migration/disaggregation idea for recurrent spec state.

title: Optimizing Speculative Decoding for Serving Large Language Models Using Goodput (SmartSpec)
quote: under higher request rates or low speculation accuracy, it paradoxically increases latency
proves: In vLLM with continuous batching, fixed speculation can raise latency under high load; SmartSpec picks a per-request length from 0 (spec off) to many tokens by estimating goodput, cutting average latency up to 3.2x vs no spec.
does_not_prove: Goodput model is per step and per request; does not account for draft KV memory reducing admitted batch, preemption, or chunked-prefill sharing. v1 results superseded by v3 (B2).
bearing: Supports per-request spec on/off as known territory; threatens any 'adaptive K by load' novelty claim.

title: TurboSpec: Closed-loop Speculation Control System for Optimizing LLM Serving Goodput
quote: automatically profiles the execution environment
proves: SmartSpec v3 renamed TurboSpec: offline profiling plus online feedback picks speculation level maximizing predicted goodput in vLLM; claims consistent gains across workloads and hardware.
does_not_prove: No venue listed; abstract gives no number; controller targets speculation level only, not admission or memory split between draft state and target KV.
bearing: Threatens closed-loop K controller ideas; leaves memory-aware admission open.

title: Speculative Decoding: Performance or Illusion?
venue: arXiv preprint (v2 Mar 2026; MLSys 2026 per search, venue not on abs page)
quote: the speedup of EAGLE over the non-SD baseline decreases from 1.73x to 1.21x as the batch size increases from 1 to 128
proves: In vLLM, EAGLE speedup on Llama3.1-8B GSM8K falls 1.73x to 1.21x from batch 1 to batch 128; verification is 42-95% of runtime; oracle adaptive combinations show up to 2.2x further headroom over the best fixed strategy.
does_not_prove: Oracle headroom ignores predictor cost and EAGLE KV maintenance; paper does not report its own crossover batch where SD is slower; quote has 'x' for the times sign.
bearing: Negative/workload result: shrinks gains at high batch size; supports a lightweight per-position predictor gap.

title: MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
venue: arXiv preprint (v5 Apr 2025; ICLR 2025 per search)
quote: Speculative decoding (SD) is a widely used technique to reduce latency losslessly
proves: At moderate-to-long contexts the KV cache dominates step cost, so SD with a sparse-KV draft still speeds up batch 32-256 serving (up to 2.51x Llama3.1-8B).
does_not_prove: Gain depends on long context where the target is memory-bound on KV; says nothing about short-context high batch or admission control; abs page lists no venue.
bearing: Supports long-context exception to 'spec hurts at high batch'; threatens claims that high batch always kills SD.

title: EAGLE-3: Scaling up Inference Acceleration of Large Language Models via Training-Time Test
quote: EAGLE reduces throughput at a batch size of 24
proves: In SGLang on H100 Llama3.1-8B MT-Bench, EAGLE is 0.93x at batch 24 while EAGLE-3 is 1.38x at batch 64; in vLLM EAGLE drops to 0.71x at batch 56 and EAGLE-3 to 1.01x.
does_not_prove: Short context, single model, one dataset; hardware labeling inconsistent (RTX3090 vs A100); no scheduler-level adaptation.
bearing: Negative result: concrete crossover batch where spec turns into slowdown.

title: AdaServe: Accelerating Multi-SLO LLM Serving with SLO-Customized Speculative Decoding
quote: reduces SLO violations by up to 4.3x and improves goodput
proves: Builds a per-request speculation tree sized to each request's latency SLO with a speculate-select-verify pipeline; up to 4.3x fewer SLO violations and 1.9x goodput vs best baselines.
does_not_prove: Per-step token allocation, not admission control; does not model draft KV memory or preemption cost; 'x' substituted for times sign in quote.
bearing: Threatens SLO-aware per-request spec budget ideas.

title: SpecServe: Efficient and SLO-Aware Large Language Model Serving with Adaptive Speculative Decoding (v2 retitled AdaSpec)
quote: existing speculative decoding solutions often fail to adapt to varying workloads and system environments
proves: Adjusts speculation strategy to real-time load with a theoretical efficiency model; claims 1.14x-14.3x over SOTA speculative systems while meeting SLOs.
does_not_prove: The 14.3x upper figure is dropped from v2; baseline choice unclear from abstract.
bearing: Threatens load-adaptive SLO-aware spec ideas.

title: SpecDec++: Boosting Speculative Decoding via Adaptive Candidate Lengths
quote: Our adaptive method achieves a 2.04x speedup on the Alpaca dataset
proves: Trained acceptance-prediction head with threshold stop rule (MDP-optimal); 2.04x on Alpaca, only 7.2% over fixed-K baseline (9.4% GSM8K, 11.1% HumanEval).
does_not_prove: Batch size 1 style evaluation, single 7B/70B pair; no serving batch effects.
bearing: Negative-ish: per-request adaptive K gives roughly 7-11% over tuned fixed K.

title: Dynamic Speculation Lookahead Accelerates Speculative Decoding of Large Language Models (DISCO)
venue: arXiv preprint (v5 Nov 2024; NeurIPS 2024 ENLSP workshop per search)
quote: DISCO reaches an average speedup of 10% compared to the best static SL baseline
proves: A classifier choosing speculation length per iteration gives about 10% average over the best static length, output identical.
does_not_prove: Single-request setting; no batching or serving load.
bearing: Negative result: dynamic length gain over best static is small (~10%).

title: AdaEDL: Early Draft Stopping for Speculative Decoding of Large Language Models via an Entropy-based Lower Bound on Token Acceptance Probability
quote: other training-free draft-stopping techniques by upto 10% in a variety of settings and datasets
proves: Training-free entropy-based draft stop beats static draft length by 10-57% and other training-free stoppers by up to 10%.
does_not_prove: Gains largest when drafting is expensive; no batch-level or server-load evaluation.
bearing: Shows per-request stop rules are crowded and the margin among them is small.

title: BanditSpec: Adaptive Speculative Decoding via Bandit Algorithms
quote: the throughput is close to the oracle best hyperparameter
proves: UCB/EXP3 bandits choose spec hyperparameters online, training-free, with regret bounds; throughput near the oracle-best fixed hyperparameter in simulated serving.
does_not_prove: 'Close to oracle best fixed' implies adaptive selection mostly recovers the best static choice rather than beating it; serving is simulated.
bearing: Negative-ish: bounds the value of online K selection to about the best fixed K.

title: Nightjar: Dynamic Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models Serving
quote: offloads the draft model to the CPU only under GPU memory pressure
proves: Bandit planner picks K per batch size, disables spec under high load, and offloads the draft to CPU to reclaim KV for larger batches; up to 14.76% throughput and 20.18% lower latency vs standard SD; defines C_switch as KV-reconstruction overhead of re-enabling spec.
does_not_prove: Small consumer/datacenter GPUs and small drafts; says restart cost of speculation was previously unquantified; does not study preemption interaction.
bearing: Closest prior art to memory-aware admission with draft overhead and spec on/off switching cost; threatens that candidate.

title: Adaptive verification (vLLM docs)
quote: the highest-scoring slots are admitted until a global budget is spent
proves: vLLM ranks every (request, position) draft slot by survival probability across the batch and admits slots up to a global token budget chosen by startup profiling to maximize accepted tokens per second.
does_not_prove: No numbers on the page; needs a confidence head and full cudagraphs; not with LoRA or pipeline parallelism; budget is per step, not tied to admission or prefill.
bearing: Threatens cross-request verification-budget allocation ideas; it is in upstream vLLM.

title: Adaptive Verification in vLLM: DSpark confidence-scheduled verification (blog)
quote: the last drafted token of a 7-token block survives less than 10% of the time
proves: On DeepSeek-V4-Pro (TP8, 8xB300), adaptive verification (PR #47808) keeps speculation beneficial up to concurrency 256 while fixed k>=5 loses; adds varlen decode CUDA graphs.
does_not_prove: Numbers only in figures; one large MoE model on top hardware; small-GPU regime not shown.
bearing: Strongly threatens 'spec hurts at high batch, fix by scheduling' ideas on big hardware.

title: Dynamic speculative decoding (vLLM v0.28.0 docs)
quote: DSD helps by tuning the K to an optimal value such that we continue to reap the benefits from SD.
proves: vLLM supports num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size: a static table of [start_bs, end_bs, K], K=0 allowed; auto-disabled with data parallelism; MRv1 piecewise cudagraph only.
does_not_prove: Static offline table, no per-request or acceptance feedback; no benchmark numbers; not verified whether present unchanged in vLLM 0.31.0 or vllm-metal.
bearing: Shows per-batch-size K and spec-off are already shipped; gap is per-request or memory-aware.

title: Adaptive speculative decoding (SGLang docs)
quote: Tier switch happens after the current round completes. Backends and CUDA graphs are never swapped mid-round.
proves: SGLang switches speculative_num_steps among tiers (default [1,3,7]) using an EMA (alpha 0.2) of batch-average accepted length, tracked per batch-size range; EAGLE/EAGLE3 with topk=1 only.
does_not_prove: Batch-level not per-request; no benchmark numbers; no hard spec-off at large batch.
bearing: Shows batch-level adaptive K is shipped in SGLang; per-request remains open there.

title: An Interpretable Latency Model for Speculative Decoding in LLM Serving
quote: explains why speedups often diminish as server load increases
proves: Analytical latency model fitted to vLLM measurements across drafter/verifier sizes, request rates, draft lengths and acceptance; explains shrinking speedup with load.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no numbers; model, not a scheduler.
bearing: Supports using an analytic model to predict when spec should be off; threatens 'new cost model' novelty.

title: ECHO: Elastic Speculative Decoding with Sparse Gating for High-Concurrency Scenarios
quote: Existing evaluations typically overlook the compute-bound nature of high-concurrency regimes
proves: Budget-aware sparse gating reallocates tree verification budget across requests under high load; claims up to 5.35x walltime speedup and over 20% relative gain over SOTA.
does_not_prove: Venue not listed; 5.35x likely at low load; kernel compatibility details not checked.
bearing: Threatens cross-request verification budget ideas at high concurrency.

title: Semi-Clairvoyant Scheduling of Speculative Decoding Requests to Minimize LLM Inference Latency (LAPS-SD)
quote: LAPS-SD reduces inference latency by approximately 39% compared to state-of-the-art scheduling methods
proves: Request-level scheduler for SD that accounts for unpredictable acceptance-driven run times instead of output length alone; ~39% lower latency.
does_not_prove: Request ordering only; no admission against draft memory; baselines are schedulers, not SD controllers.
bearing: Threatens SD-aware request ordering ideas.

title: Adaptive Resource Allocation for Low-Latency LLM Serving (RIKEN AIP poster, Takamaeda team)
quote: Optimal aggressiveness of Speculative Decoding and Chunked Prefill depends on the request rate
proves: Jointly picks number of candidate tokens and chunked-prefill token budget to minimize TPOT under a TTFT constraint, on Vicuna 7B-33B, A100; dynamic beats any fixed setting.
does_not_prove: Poster only, no numbers in extracted text; title read from extracted PDF text; not peer reviewed.
bearing: Only source found on verification vs prefill token-budget sharing; supports that this joint area is thin.

title: FastGRPO: Accelerating Policy Optimization via Concurrency-aware Speculative Decoding and Online Draft Learning
quote: concurrency-aware speculative decoding framework that dynamically adjusts the drafting and verification strategy
proves: Direct SD in GRPO gives limited speedup at high concurrency; adapting draft/verify to live concurrency plus online draft learning gives 2.35x-2.72x end-to-end.
does_not_prove: Math reasoning only; no general serving admission.
bearing: Threatens 'spec as concurrency drops in RL rollout' ideas.

title: Fast LLM Post-training via Decoupled and Fastest-of-N Speculation (SpecActor)
quote: applying vanilla speculative decoding to rollout yields only 10 % speedup at worst on common production configurations
proves: At per-worker batch 128-256 (production GRPO/DAPO traces on 256 GPUs) vanilla SD gives no or negative gain; decoupled speculation plus Fastest-of-N drafts gives 2.0-2.4x mean rollout speed.
does_not_prove: Specific to RL rollout; batch shrinks during rollout, so gain concentrates in the tail.
bearing: Negative result for high-batch spec; supports tail-phase spec in rollouts.

title: Beat the long tail: Distribution-Aware Speculative Decoding for RL Training (DAS)
quote: reduces rollout time up to 50% while preserving identical training curves
proves: Suffix-tree drafter from recent rollouts plus length-aware policy that gives long trajectories larger draft budgets; up to 50% less rollout time.
does_not_prove: Nonparametric drafter only; no memory cost accounting of the suffix tree.
bearing: Threatens long-tail-aware spec budget ideas for rollouts.

title: History Rhymes: Accelerating LLM Reinforcement Learning with RhymeRL
venue: arXiv preprint (ASPLOS 26 per search, not on abs page)
quote: RhymeRL achieves a 2.6x performance improvement over existing methods
proves: HistoSpec drafts from prior-epoch rollouts; HistoPipe schedules using historical length distributions; 2.6x at dozens to thousands of GPUs.
does_not_prove: Needs a warm-up epoch (per B26); scheduling and spec gains not separated in abstract.
bearing: Threatens history-based rollout spec plus length-aware scheduling.

title: BubbleSpec: Turning Long-Tail Bubbles into Speculative Rollout Drafts for Synchronous Reinforcement Learning
quote: BubbleSpec reduces decoding steps by 50% and increases rollout throughput by up to 1.8x
proves: Uses idle time of fast DP ranks to pre-generate drafts for later steps; no warm-up epoch needed; up to 1.8x rollout throughput.
does_not_prove: Synchronous RL only; does not address serving.
bearing: Threatens idle-bubble draft generation ideas.

title: SPEC-RL: Accelerating On-Policy Reinforcement Learning with Speculative Rollouts
quote: SPEC-RL reduces rollout time by 2-3x without compromising policy quality
proves: Reuses prior-epoch trajectory segments as speculative prefixes; 2-3x rollout time reduction in PPO/GRPO/DAPO.
does_not_prove: Math benchmarks; draft source is history, not a model.
bearing: Crowds history-reuse rollout spec.

title: SRT: Accelerating Reinforcement Learning via Speculative Rollout with Tree-Structured Cache
quote: achieving up to 2.08x wall-clock time speedup during rollout
proves: Per-prompt tree cache of past continuations as model-free drafter, plus run-ahead generation in idle bubbles; up to 2.08x rollout speedup.
does_not_prove: Cache memory cost and eviction not described in abstract.
bearing: Crowds rollout spec; leaves draft-cache memory management open.

title: SPARK: Learning from Verification in Speculative GRPO Rollouts
quote: leverages target verification feedback to refine draft predictions during generation
proves: Draft misses repeat within a response and across a GRPO group; feeding verification back gives 32.7% over EAGLE3-style and 11.4% over DFlash-style generation speed, 21 settings.
does_not_prove: Drafter adaptation, not scheduling; gain over DFlash is modest.
bearing: Last-6-months check: rollout spec work is moving to drafter quality, not scheduling.

title: Llumnix: Dynamic Scheduling for Large Language Model Serving
quote: Llumnix can safely copy the KV cache of previous tokens in parallel with the computation for new tokens.
proves: Live migration relies on append-only KV; downtime is the copy of one iteration's KV, roughly 20-30 ms and constant in sequence length.
does_not_prove: No mention of speculative decoding. Rejected-token KV and draft KV are not append-only per step (writes then rollback), so the one-iteration-delta argument is unchecked for spec decode.
bearing: supports live migration of spec state as open gap

title: RLHFSpec: Breaking the Efficiency Bottleneck in RLHF Training via Adaptive Drafting
quote: the d-instance can commence the subsequent computation as soon as it receives the SSM KVCache
proves: Migrates draft (SSM=small model) and target KV separately in two stages; destination resumes drafting once draft KV arrives; combined overhead under 3.87% of execution time.
does_not_prove: RLHF rollout, not online serving; no migration-only measurement; draft model with its own KV, not EAGLE hidden states or MTP; 'near-zero' overhead claim unmeasured.
bearing: threatens novelty of draft-KV-first migration

title: Nightjar: Dynamic Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models Serving
quote: proactively disables speculative decoding
proves: Under memory strain disables spec decode and moves draft model weights to CPU to free KV; up to 14.76% throughput, 20.18% lower latency vs standard SD.
does_not_prove: Offloads draft weights, not per-request draft KV; does not address what happens to in-flight draft state of preempted requests.
bearing: partial overlap with memory-pressure-aware spec policy

title: Towards Resiliency in Large Language Model Serving with KevlarFlow
quote: background KV cache replication to maintain high throughput during partial failures
proves: Fault tolerance by replicating KV; 20x MTTR reduction (10 min to 30 s), 3.1x avg latency under failure.
does_not_prove: Abstract only read; no mention of speculative decoding, draft KV, or hidden-state replication.
bearing: supports gap: spec-aware failure recovery

title: LUMEN: Coordinated Failure Recovery for Distributed LLM Serving
quote: restore KV caches from checkpoints stored on a fixed neighboring worker
proves: Recent recovery work checkpoints KV and redistributes interrupted requests load-aware.
does_not_prove: Abstract only; no mention of speculative decoding or of whether draft state is checkpointed or rebuilt.
bearing: supports gap: spec-aware failure recovery

title: fix(v1): prevent IMA after speculative preemption (vLLM PR 49620, fixes 41190)
quote: a request can be preempted after a speculative decode frame has been dispatched but before its output returns
proves: With async scheduling, preemption mid-flight leaves stale spec output; fix discards it in units of 1+num_scheduled_spec placeholder tokens; linked crash was illegal memory access on hybrid GDN + MTP/DFlash.
does_not_prove: Open PR; fix is discard-and-recompute, so all verified-but-unreturned work is thrown away; no cost measurement of lost speculative work under preemption.
bearing: supports preemption-cost-of-spec-work candidates

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Preserve EAGLE/MTP draft KV during CPU retraction (SGLang PR 44899)
quote: separate EAGLE/MTP pools use the same token slots without being included in that backup
proves: Before this PR, SGLang PD decode retraction to CPU saved target KV but not EAGLE/MTP draft KV, so draft history was overwritten by other requests; outputs stay correct but acceptance drops.
does_not_prove: Open PR, 3 days old; explicitly excludes fused draft storage, Frozen-KV MTP, DFlash, recurrent state; no measured acceptance loss.
bearing: supports: preempt/swap of draft state is live, unmeasured

title: Preserve full DFlash draft KV during PD CPU retraction (SGLang PR 39749)
quote: the resumed request drafts against another request's KV and its acceptance rate drops
proves: Same silent acceptance loss for DFlash draft KV after retraction; host_pool backend already carries draft KV as a DRAFT sidecar pool.
does_not_prove: Open; only CPU unit tests; magnitude of acceptance loss never measured.
bearing: supports measurement candidate on silent acceptance loss

title: Fix PD retraction checkpoint boundaries with overlap decoding (SGLang PR 39743)
quote: the in-flight verify commits a whole accepted block into KV and draft state, but those tokens never reach `output_ids`
proves: With overlap scheduling, retraction checkpoint can be one step ahead: recurrent state advances twice on resume, and spec-decode requests skip tokens or end early (correctness bug).
does_not_prove: Open; a fix by draining pending results first; no general model of checkpoint consistency for spec + recurrent state.
bearing: supports checkpoint-consistency candidate

title: Fix EAGLE chunked-prefill next prompt token for resumed requests with output (SGLang PR 28254)
quote: fell back to the speculatively predicted token instead of the already-known fill token, corrupting the draft KV for that chunk
proves: Retracted-then-resumed requests re-prefill origin+output; EAGLE draft KV was rebuilt wrongly at chunk boundaries in output region.
does_not_prove: Open since June; acceptance impact not measured.
bearing: supports: recompute-on-resume path for draft state is fragile

title: [PD] Transfer EAGLE draft probabilities for rejection sampling (SGLang PR 40953)
quote: Top-k candidates alone do not provide the proposal probabilities needed by the verifier.
proves: PD handoff must carry the FP32 draft distribution for lossless stochastic rejection sampling; restricted to single-layer EAGLE.
does_not_prove: Draft PR; GPU transport and sampling quality not validated; metadata size cost reported only qualitatively.
bearing: supports spec-state transfer protocol candidates

title: fix(dflash): reject unsupported PD disaggregation (SGLang PR 36277)
quote: The existing PD wire format transfers target KV state and EAGLE-style final hidden state, but not DFLASH's per-layer draft state.
proves: SGLang PD carries EAGLE final hidden state but not DFlash per-layer draft state; combination crashed or hung, now rejected at startup.
does_not_prove: Guard, not support; no design for per-layer draft state transfer.
bearing: supports PD transfer of non-EAGLE draft state as gap

title: DSpark speculative decoding incompatible with NIXL P/D disaggregation and Hopper FA3 (vLLM issue 48221)
quote: DSpark adds `is_eagle_group=True` KV cache layers for the draft model attention. Prefill has fewer KV layers than decode.
proves: Draft KV layers must exist on both P and D; decode-only drafter fails NIXL handshake (layer count mismatch); both-sides config crashes on FA3.
does_not_prove: Open bug report; no measurement of draft KV transfer size or whether D could rebuild draft KV locally instead.
bearing: supports P-vs-D draft KV placement candidate

title: [Bugfix][Core][Spec Decode] Skip spec-decode block reservation on the external-KV-load step (P/D) (vLLM PR 50173)
quote: The prefill transfers N prompt blocks, but the scheduler will reserve N+1 (MTP1) blocks on the decode node.
proves: MTP lookahead and pad_spec_decode over-allocate on decode during KV import and trip a connector assert (DeepSeek-R1, 1P1D, MoRIIO).
does_not_prove: Bookkeeping fix only.
bearing: weak; shows lookahead slots leak into transfer accounting

title: [Core][PD] Role-aware optimizations for Spec decoding (vLLM PR 45280)
quote: P should prefill both target and drafter, D should only allocate blocks for transferring prefilled model+drafter
proves: vLLM direction: prefill instance runs drafter prefill with num_speculative_tokens=1 and no lookahead; draft KV for all layers is transferred to decode.
does_not_prove: Open; no cost comparison of transferring draft KV vs recomputing it on D.
bearing: supports transfer-vs-recompute draft KV study

title: [RFC]: Disaggregated Speculative Decoding with Standalone Parallel Draft Model (vLLM issue 42109)
quote: The target sends a *verification outcome* after each step; the draft server returns *K draft tokens per request*
proves: Proposes separate draft server with speculation cache, N:M verify/draft servers; claims draft adds 10-30% per-step latency when colocated.
does_not_prove: RFC with internal POC; no failure, migration, or preemption handling for draft server state described.
bearing: adjacent; draft-server failure/migration open

title: Dynamo Known Issues (v1.3.0: Disagg Decode + EAGLE3 Speculative Decoding Crashes Silently)
quote: In a disaggregated deployment, EAGLE3 speculative decoding crashes silently under large KV-transfer volume
proves: EAGLE3 + PD on vLLM backend was unsupported in Dynamo v1.3.0, fix targeted v1.4.0.
does_not_prove: Root cause not stated; whether fixed upstream not shown.
bearing: shows PD+EAGLE fragility in production stacks

title: [Bugfix][V1] Retain the EAGLE hit blocks below a sliding window across a KV connector import (vLLM PR 61011)
quote: Every later request whose prompt is longer than the window misses on all layers
proves: On P/D decode, imported SWA DFlash draft group has 32 blocks but EAGLE hit needs 33; zero draft hit zeroes the target hit too.
does_not_prove: Prefix-cache hit-rate loss not quantified in throughput.
bearing: supports draft-KV-aware cache/transfer design

title: [Fix] hicache: Count the EAGLE bigram boundary token in PD decode restores (SGLang PR 45076)
quote: every request that hits L2 or L3 is aborted ("HiCache restore failed")
proves: EAGLE radix keys are bigrams (N positions keyed by N+1 tokens); restore from host/storage tiers off-by-one aborted every L2/L3 hit in PD decode.
does_not_prove: One-line fix; shows tiered restore and EAGLE keying interact, not cost.
bearing: supports offload/restore + spec as active bug area

title: [RFC]: Lookahead-aware prefix-cache hashing for EAGLE-style draft models (vLLM issue 50438)
quote: all of these EAGLE-style draft methods conservatively drop the last matched unit and recompute it
proves: EAGLE draft KV at a block boundary depends on the next token, so cached draft KV is not keyed by block tokens alone; vLLM drops one block per hit.
does_not_prove: RFC; no measured cost of the dropped block.
bearing: supports draft-KV keying for restore/migration

title: [Bug]: [SpecDecode] Hybrid Mamba (align) corrupts under speculative decoding when a KV connector is attached (vLLM issue 53505)
quote: Hybrid Mamba (align) corrupts under speculative decoding when a KV connector is attached — even with zero retrieved tokens
proves: Hybrid Mamba + spec decode + KV connector produced corrupted output.
does_not_prove: Closed; quote is the issue title; body mostly environment; root cause addressed partly by PR 54165.
bearing: shows hybrid+spec+offload correctness fragility

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Restore hybrid mamba align cache hits under spec decode with a KV connector (vLLM PR 54165)
quote: misclassify DFlash/DSpark as eagle-family drafters and corrupt or degrade the mamba align prefix cache
proves: Three deterministic defects on spec + hybrid mamba + KV connector path; drafter type changes which block is safe to restore.
does_not_prove: Did not reproduce the LMCache corruption; related, not full fix.
bearing: supports drafter-aware restore semantics

title: Garbage output with MTP speculative decoding on long prompts (LMCache issue 4345)
quote: When MTP speculative decoding is enabled (num_speculative_tokens=2), LMCache returns corrupt KV tensors for long prompts.
proves: Silent garbage output with LMCache + MTP on ~3000-token prompts; disabling LMCache fixes it.
does_not_prove: Open; root cause unknown in body read.
bearing: shows offload+spec correctness gap

title: [BUG] Hybrid Mamba/GDN + MTP5: mixed local+external prefix hit ... deterministic spec-decode degeneration (LMCache issue 5675)
quote: the resumed recurrent state behaves **prompt-independent**, i.e. most likely **all-zero / never written** rather than stale
proves: Mixed local+external prefix hit on GDN hybrid + MTP5 gives acceptance exactly 1.00 (0/~1100 drafted accepted) and garbage output.
does_not_prove: Open; root cause not found; single setup on 2080Ti.
bearing: supports recurrent-state restore + spec as unsolved

title: [Bug]: CPU offloading fails with block_size=256 + speculative decoding due to eagle group block_size mismatch (vLLM issue 48919)
quote: CPU offloading fails with block_size=256 + speculative decoding due to eagle group block_size mismatch
proves: Draft (eagle group) KV has its own block geometry that the CPU offload connector does not handle; crash at init; works with block_size=128.
does_not_prove: Config bug, not a design study.
bearing: weak; draft KV as distinct offload object

title: ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State
quote: rolling back rejected draft tokens only requires removing their buffer entries
proves: vLLM's baseline stores a separate SSM state per speculative token; caching inputs instead gives 1.87-1.96x over standard decode, up to 2.14x over baseline spec path, 3.0-3.3x more concurrent requests.
does_not_prove: No mention of preemption, prefix caching, or PD; replay ring is new per-request state that must survive those.
bearing: threatens per-position-checkpoint candidates; opens ring-state lifecycle

title: [WIP][ReplaySSM] Support prefix caching for GDN speculative decode (vLLM PR 56466)
quote: keep ReplaySSM metadata and cursors consistent across cache hits, block reuse and preemption
proves: Prototype makes replay ring survive prefix caching and preemption; 360/360 requests, 585 real preemptions, zero errors (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, MTP=3, 2xH200).
does_not_prove: WIP; correctness only, no cost of preemption with ring state; not PD or migration.
bearing: partially closes hybrid spec preemption

title: [Spec Decode][Qwen3.5] RecoverSSM for Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next GDN (vLLM PR 61309)
quote: +8.6% output throughput at K=5
proves: RecoverSSM verify/commit path for Qwen GDN + MTP; +8.6% throughput at K=5, c=32 on Qwen3.5-4B, L40S, acceptance unchanged.
does_not_prove: Open; small model; interaction with preemption/offload not covered.
bearing: rollback mechanism is moving fast upstream

title: [Feat] [NVIDIA] mamba2: Add compact speculative-state replay (SGLang PR 41968)
quote: Reduce Mamba2 speculative-decoding memory by replacing full candidate-state snapshots with compact input records.
proves: SGLang port of replay idea for Mamba2 spec; explicitly unsupported with PD disaggregation, adaptive/ragged verification, int8 checkpoints.
does_not_prove: SM100 only, topk 1, 4 verify positions.
bearing: supports PD/adaptive + replay-state as open

title: [Fix] pd: Size decode Mamba spec-state scratch by running batch, not decode extra slots (SGLang PR 44015)
quote: `intermediate_ssm_state_cache` is **20.5 GB** instead of **7.4 GB** per GPU
proves: Per-draft-position SSM scratch is fp32 [layers, slots+1, draft_tokens, ...]; on PD decode it was sized for in-transfer slots, 20.5 GB vs 7.4 GB per GPU, causing OOM.
does_not_prove: Sizing fix; shows memory scale of per-position checkpoints, not a policy.
bearing: supports memory cost of recurrent rollback state

title: [Performance]: Avoidable preemption at hybrid Attention/Mamba decode block transitions (vLLM issue 62752)
quote: The remaining capacity then forces preemption, although an alternative order completes all requests without preemption at the same pool size.
proves: CPU reproducer: with aligned Mamba + 5 spec tokens + 5 lookahead slots, FCFS block consumption causes avoidable preemptions.
does_not_prove: Opened today; simulated outputs; no throughput measurement.
bearing: supports spec-aware admission/preemption policy candidate

title: STree: Speculative Tree Decoding for Hybrid State-Space Models
quote: extending speculative decoding to SSMs require backtracking the state, which is non-trivial at scale.
proves: Tree spec decoding for SSM/hybrid via accumulated transition matrices; 1.74-1.98x (temp 0) on RTX 3090 vs 1.69-1.93x vanilla SD; slightly slower than vanilla at temp 0 on H100.
does_not_prove: Single-request kernel study; no serving, preemption, or batching of rollback state.
bearing: rollback algorithm known; serving lifecycle open

title: The Mamba in the Llama: Distilling and Accelerating Hybrid Models
quote: The approach maintains only one RNN hidden state in cache for verification.
proves: Snapshot state before drafting and recompute on rejection; 2.1-2.6x on 3090, 1.71-2x on H100; naive version no speedup on H100.
does_not_prove: Single request; no serving-system state lifecycle.
bearing: prior art for snapshot+recompute rollback

title: SpecMamba: Accelerating Mamba Inference on FPGA with Speculative Decoding
quote: Mamba discards previous hidden states after each update, complicating state recovery when draft tokens are rejected.
proves: Names the two rollback options (store per-draft states vs cache activations and recompute); storing is prohibitive for target model.
does_not_prove: FPGA, not GPU serving.
bearing: frames store-vs-recompute tradeoff

title: H-Spec: Parallel Speculative Decoding Without a Drafter-Side KV Cache
quote: Drafter-side KV introduces additional GPU memory overhead.
proves: Block drafters (DFlash-style) keep a separate drafter KV: per-token KV rises 1.139x (Qwen3-4B, 144 KiB target + 20 KiB draft), 1.156x (Llama3.1-8B), 1.375x (Qwen3.5-27B), 1.8x (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B); drafter KV injection time grows 4.7x from 4 to 128 concurrent requests (Qwen3-8B); reusing target KV in place cuts KV utilization 4.3-24.6% and lifts peak throughput 5-17%.
does_not_prove: Draft overhead fraction grows as target KV shrinks (hybrid/MLA/GDN targets), but no study of how draft KV interacts with prefix caching, eviction, or offload tiers.
bearing: Supports draft-KV-elimination ideas; shows draft KV share is largest on hybrid models

title: Strong Drafts Need Compact Memories: Long-Context Speculative Decoding with Compressed KV Cache
quote: reduces draft-side memory by over 70%
proves: Independent drafter with adaptor-compressed KV cuts draft-side memory >70% with up to 2.08x (Llama3.1-8B) and 3.33x (70B) speedup at prefixes up to 32K.
does_not_prove: Single-request long-context focus; no batching, prefix-cache sharing or tiering of the compressed draft memory.
bearing: Threatens naive 'compress draft KV' candidates; already done

title: When Hidden States Drift: Can KV Caches Rescue Long-Range Speculative Decoding?
quote: KV-Reuse improves long-range acceptance, although end-to-end speedups remain marginal under current training pipelines.
proves: Letting an EAGLE-style drafter read the target KV (KVShot: hidden-only vs KV-only vs hybrid) raises long-range acceptance on Qwen3-8B but end-to-end speedup is marginal.
does_not_prove: Algorithmic study; no memory or serving-system accounting of drafter reading target KV.
bearing: Weakens 'draft reuses target KV for accuracy' as a speed win; memory angle open

title: vllm-metal: Speculative decoding
quote: Its committed KV and speculative lookahead share the Metal KV memory budget with the target.
proves: On the user's own backend, draft-model KV and lookahead share the target's Metal KV budget, no separate draft scratch pool; MTP reads target KV (no extra KV); with align-mode prefix caching drafts are capped at the state-block boundary. Methods: MTP, draft model, N-gram; DFlash/DSpark experimental.
does_not_prove: A search snippet of an earlier version said the draft KV cache was 'un-budgeted'; the current page says budgeted. No numbers on how much of the budget the draft takes.
bearing: Directly testable on M5 16 GB; supports measuring draft share of KV budget

title: [RFC]: Lookahead-aware prefix-cache hashing for EAGLE-style draft models (vLLM #50438)
quote: all of these EAGLE-style draft methods conservatively drop the last matched unit and recompute it.
proves: vLLM drops the last prefix-cache block for all use_eagle() methods because the draft input at a block boundary depends on the next token; one Qwen3.6 report (v0.20.1) saw hit rate fall 87.3% -> 69.9%, 1,056 fewer hit tokens per request. RFC proposes hashing one following token.
does_not_prove: Open RFC, not merged; cost on non-hybrid (16-token block) models is small and unmeasured here.
bearing: Supports 'spec-aware prefix cache keys' gap; also shows engines already working on it

title: [Bug/Perf]: the dense default chosen for Mamba + EAGLE reverts to 0% prefix reuse under interleaved long conversations (vLLM #58303)
quote: Under interleaved long conversations the pool fills, the attention chains get evicted, and prefix reuse returns to a clean **0%**
proves: Hybrid GDN + EAGLE/DFlash2 on RTX 5090: dense recurrent-state checkpoints (default chosen because EAGLE tail-block drop makes sparse retention unreachable) fill the pool; two alternating ~135K conversations get 0% reuse (55-65 s re-prefill) vs 97-99% with a 1-in-6 interval. Mamba page holds speculative state slots so block size moves with draft count (2176 at 7 drafts, 2432 at 15).
does_not_prove: Single reporter rig, hybrid models only; no policy study.
bearing: Strong support for spec-decode x prefix-cache capacity/eviction gap on hybrid models

title: EAGLE/MTP block drop + prefix caching is untested for hybrid models with >=3 attention groups (vLLM #51771)
quote: We hit a **total (0.0%) prefix-cache loss** on this configuration
proves: DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark (4 attention groups): with EAGLE block drop on, 5-turn agentic session hit rate 0.0% vs 72.7% with drop disabled, wall clock 64.27 s vs 30.61 s, acceptance length 4.80 vs 4.76. CI covers at most 2 attention groups.
does_not_prove: Reported on a fork base; authors think main is fine for this shape. Test-coverage issue.
bearing: Supports gap: spec decode silently breaks prefix reuse; correctness/coverage tooling

title: [Bug] EAGLE speculative decoding defeats radix prefix reuse for multi-turn traffic (SGLang #32459)
quote: Enabling EAGLE speculative decoding collapses radix prefix reuse for multi-turn agentic traffic
proves: SGLang v0.5.16, GLM-5.2 NVFP4 8xB200: deep-prompt cache hit 97% without spec vs 53%/40% with EAGLE; input throughput 43,981 vs 12,881-16,811 tok/s; TTFT p50 0.54 s vs 2.15-2.68 s. HiCache on/off no effect. Candidate fix #32574 unmerged; issue stale-closed.
does_not_prove: One model family; root cause not confirmed.
bearing: Supports gap in SGLang radix cache + EAGLE; shows cost is TTFT not decode

title: [Bug] HiCache draft KV pool backup crashes with cudaMemcpyBatchAsync invalid argument in PD disaggregation (SGLang #31252)
quote: the draft KV pool's host backup crashes
proves: SGLang HiCache keeps a separate host-tier backup for the draft KV pool (mem_pool_host_draft) alongside the target pool; with PD + HiCache + EAGLE the draft-pool backup crashes (regression v0.5.14 -> v0.5.15).
does_not_prove: Bug report only; no data on host memory used by draft pool or its hit value.
bearing: Shows draft KV is tiered to CPU in SGLang; supports tiering-policy questions

title: HybridKVCacheCoordinator: DSpark draft-model KV-cache group's ephemeral content incorrectly vetoes GPU-tier prefix cache reuse (vLLM #48455)
quote: It is a write-then-immediately-consume-within-round buffer, not an incrementally accumulated, reusable cache
proves: vLLM requires every KV group to hit; DSpark's draft group is rewritten each round from target hidden states, so it vetoes prefix reuse of the target's groups, including on resume after preemption. Contrasts with EAGLE/MTP draft KV, which is reusable.
does_not_prove: Open bug; no hit-rate numbers on GPU tier.
bearing: Supports taxonomy gap: which draft state is cacheable vs ephemeral

title: [Bug]: OffloadingConnector: DSpark draft-model KV-cache group's sparse storage causes external_prefix_cache_hits_total to be permanently 0 (vLLM #47890)
quote: the external (RAM-tier) prefix cache **never records a hit**
proves: With CPU offloading, the draft group's stored blocks are sparse, so the AND-lookup returns 0 for every request even though target groups alone reach 88.9-100% hit rate, while offload store bytes grow into hundreds of GB.
does_not_prove: Specific to DSpark + OffloadingConnector; open.
bearing: Supports gap: offload tiers not designed for draft KV

title: [Bug]: Gemma 4 MTP + NIXL PD disaggregation - draft model KV not transferred, MTP ineffective (vLLM #54926)
quote: the draft model's KV state built during prefill is never transferred to the decode pod
proves: In vLLM PD disaggregation, draft KV groups are excluded from NIXL transfer; decode pod recomputes 15k+ tokens through draft heads per request at ISL=15k.
does_not_prove: No measured TTFT/throughput cost given.
bearing: Supports migration/transfer of draft state as an open systems gap

title: Nightjar: Dynamic Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models Serving
quote: reduces KV cache capacity, limiting batch size and degrading throughput
proves: Keeping the draft model resident costs KV capacity; Nightjar offloads the draft to CPU when spec is disabled under memory pressure: up to 14.76% higher throughput and 20.18% lower latency.
does_not_prove: Moves whole draft model, not draft KV; abstract-level evidence.
bearing: Threatens 'offload draft when idle' candidate; already done

title: AdaSpec: Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Fast, SLO-Aware Large Language Model Serving
quote: equal parts, allocating one for the KV Cache of the draft model and the other for the KV Cache of the target model.
proves: Describes (older) vLLM lookahead scheduler splitting memory equally between draft and target KV caches.
does_not_prove: Refers to older vLLM; current V1 behavior not shown by this source.
bearing: Historic baseline for draft KV sizing; do not cite as current

title: SuffixDecoding: Extreme Speculative Decoding for Emerging AI Applications
quote: utilizes efficient suffix trees to cache long token sequences from prompts and previous outputs
proves: Model-free suffix-tree drafting caching prompts and prior outputs: up to 5.3x speedup, 2.8x over EAGLE-2/3, 1.9x over Token Recycling, on agentic SWE-Bench and Text-to-SQL.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no tree memory or CPU cost and no hit rates versus cache size.
bearing: Threatens basic cross-request draft cache ideas; leaves cache sizing/eviction open

title: Arctic Inference: Suffix Decoding docs
quote: Currently, only FIFO eviction is implemented.
proves: Global suffix tree of completed outputs plus per-request tree; suffix_cache_max_requests default 100000, FIFO eviction only; higher depth costs memory. Suffix alone: 286 vs 75.8 tok/s on SWE-Bench, 113 vs 76.0 on ShareGPT (vLLM 0.8.4).
does_not_prove: No memory size numbers, no hit-rate vs capacity curve, no tenant isolation.
bearing: Supports gap in eviction/admission policy for cross-request draft caches

title: SuffixDecoding at Production Scale with Arctic Inference and vLLM
quote: reduced memory by 2.3x
proves: Custom hashmap cut tree memory 2.3x and sped speculation 3.4x; original CPU cost 20-30 us/token, residual overhead about 10% at concurrency 64; original version was worse than n-gram at concurrency 64; 1.96-3.12x on BlazeEdit, 1.0-1.28x on SpecBench.
does_not_prove: No absolute tree size or hit-rate data.
bearing: Shows CPU-side draft cache cost matters at high batch size

title: [RFC]: Suffix decoding on GPU (suffix_gpu) - GPU-resident suffix decoding compatible with async scheduling (vLLM #51788)
quote: `method="suffix"` forces `--no-async-scheduling` today
proves: CPU suffix drafter needs committed host token ids, so it is excluded from async scheduling; RFC moves suffix automaton plus a cross-request global index onto GPU (capacity knobs suffix_gpu_global_capacity, delta_capacity).
does_not_prove: Proposal; GPU memory cost of the global index not quantified in the part read.
bearing: Supports question of where draft caches should live (CPU vs GPU memory)

title: REST: Retrieval-Based Speculative Decoding
quote: results in a datastore with a size of 27GB
proves: Datastore sizes: 27 GB code (The Stack), 12 GB chat (UltraChat), 465 MB ShareGPT; retrieval 0.1-0.7 ms per token (<1 ms); 1.62-2.36x speedup at batch 1.
does_not_prove: Batch 1 only; static datastore; no tiering or update policy.
bearing: Baseline for size of retrieval draft caches; CPU/SSD placement open

title: Turning Trash into Treasure: Accelerating Inference of Large Language Models with Token Recycling
quote: requires \textless2MB of additional storage
proves: Adjacency matrix of past candidate tokens costs <2 MB and gives about 2x speedup across model sizes.
does_not_prove: No cross-request or multi-tenant sharing analysis.
bearing: Shows small draft caches suffice; weakens memory-pressure motivation for n-gram pools

title: Cacheback: Speculative Decoding With Nothing But Cache
quote: a fully populated table uses at most a few GiB of DRAM
proves: LRU n-gram tables (leader capacity 2^20, follower capacity 128) up to a few GiB DRAM; 1.86x on SpecBench Vicuna-7B with dynamic+frozen tables vs 1.64x dynamic only, 1.28x frozen only.
does_not_prove: No hit-rate numbers; dynamic cache is per task, not shared across requests.
bearing: Supports LRU-vs-FIFO and cross-request sharing as open questions

title: Break the Sequential Dependency of LLM Inference Using Lookahead Decoding
quote: without needing auxiliary models or data stores
proves: Lookahead decoding: up to 1.8x on MT-bench, 4x with strong scaling on code completion, no auxiliary model or datastore.
does_not_prove: Abstract has no n-gram pool size or memory numbers.
bearing: Background for n-gram pool candidates

title: When Speculation Spills Secrets: Side Channels via Speculative Decoding In LLMs
quote: confidential datastore contents used for prediction
proves: Observers can fingerprint queries (>75% at T=0.3 over 50 prompts) across four spec schemes incl. vLLM, and leak datastore contents at >25 tokens/s; mitigations: packet padding, iteration-wise token aggregation.

title: QuantSpec: Self-Speculative Decoding with Hierarchical Quantized KV Cache
quote: employs a hierarchical 4-bit quantized KV cache and 4-bit quantized weights for acceleration

bearing: Threatens 'quantized KV draft' candidates; already done

title: MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
quote: SD can achieve speedup even for a high throughput inference regime for moderate to long sequences
proves: Sparse-KV draft gives up to 2.51x for Llama3.1-8B at batch 32-256 because KV, not weights, dominates at long context and large batch.
does_not_prove: Speedup depends on long sequences; short-context large-batch regime not helped.

title: Vegas: Self-Speculative Decoding with Verification-Guided Sparse Attention
quote: speedup in decoding throughput over default vLLM
proves: Drafts with sparse attention over KV entries found critical during verification; 1.25-2.81x decode throughput over default vLLM, 1.15-1.29x over prior sparse self-spec.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not state memory cost or prefix-cache behavior.
bearing: Threatens sparse self-spec candidates in vLLM

title: LayerSkip: Enabling Early Exit Inference and Self-Speculative Decoding
quote: has less memory footprint than other speculative decoding approaches
proves: Early-exit self-spec shares compute and activations (one KV cache) between draft and verify; up to 2.16x on CNN/DM, 1.82x coding.
does_not_prove: Needs special training; not a serving-system study.
bearing: Background for 'no separate draft KV' designs

title: SpecExec: Massively Parallel Speculative Decoding for Interactive LLM Inference on Consumer Devices
quote: we keep the past key/value caches of both draft and main models in GPU memory at all times
proves: Offloaded Llama 2-70B: 4-6 tok/s 4-bit, 2-3 tok/s 16-bit, up to 20 tokens per target iteration with draft budgets up to 2048; both KV caches kept on GPU, draft caches only needed during drafting.
does_not_prove: Batch 1; KV placement under memory limits only sketched.
bearing: Threatens spec-for-offload candidates; draft KV placement under offload open

title: Speculate Deep and Accurate: Lossless and Training-Free Acceleration for Offloaded LLMs via Substitute Speculative Decoding (SubSpec)
quote: delivering 9.1x speedup for Qwen2.5 7B on MT-Bench (8GB VRAM limit)
proves: Draft built from low-bit substitutes of offloaded layers; 9.1x Qwen2.5-7B (8 GB VRAM), average 12.5x Qwen2.5-32B (24 GB).
does_not_prove: Discrete GPU + PCIe setting, not unified memory like Apple silicon.
bearing: Threatens offload-spec candidates on discrete GPUs

title: ShadowSpec: Towards Zero Speculation Overhead for Substitute Speculative Decoding
quote: 17–54% end-to-end speedup over the SubSpec baseline
proves: Overlaps draft tree extension with PCIe loading of offloaded target weights: 17-54% over SubSpec on a consumer GPU.
does_not_prove: Workshop poster; PCIe-specific.
bearing: Shows offload-spec line is active as of 2026

title: Dovetail: A CPU/GPU Heterogeneous Speculative Decoding for LLM inference
quote: inference speedups ranging from 1.79x to 10.1x across different devices
proves: Draft on GPU, target on CPU: 1.79-10.1x on 13B models across devices.
does_not_prove: No memory figures on the page.
bearing: Background for heterogeneous placement

title: SGLang docs: Speculative Decoding
quote: the draft tree, CUDA graphs, and verification-related buffers consume additional VRAM
proves: SGLang has no separate draft memory knob; --mem-fraction-static covers weights + KV pool; NGRAM cache --speculative-ngram-capacity default 10,000,000 entries, max trie depth 18; NGRAM disables overlap scheduler and mixed chunked prefill.

title: Speculative Decoding: Performance or Illusion?

does_not_prove: Abstract says nothing on memory effects.

title: A Sparse Glimpse of the Whole: Train-Free Self-Speculative Decoding (SparseSpec-L)
quote: without permanently discarding the dense KV cache

does_not_prove: No memory numbers on abstract page; speedup value missing from page text.
bearing: Threatens sparse-KV self-spec novelty (last 6 months)

title: vllm-ascend issue #9247 (DeepSeek-V4 MTP halves prefix-cache hit length)
proves: Search snippet only: enabling MTP cut prefix-cache hit length from 32768 to 16384 tokens due to EAGLE last-block drop plus alignment rounding.
does_not_prove: Not opened; numbers unverified.

title: Speculative Decoding (vLLM docs, latest)
quote: vLLM does not currently guarantee stable token log probabilities (logprobs).
proves: vLLM lists EAGLE, LiLiCorr, MTP, draft model, PARD, n-gram, suffix, hidden-state extraction, custom proposer, dynamic SD, adaptive verification, lossy FLy verification and per-request acceptance metrics as spec features
does_not_prove: The docs say nothing about how spec decode interacts with prefix caching, chunked prefill, preemption or async scheduling. Those rules live only in code and issues

title: Dynamic Speculative Decoding (vLLM docs)
quote: K=0 will be used when the concurrency is in range [129, 512], i.e., no draft tokens will be produced.
proves: vLLM dynamic SD is a user-supplied batch-size to K table. It was tested with Eagle, Eagle-3 and DFlash, gets full CUDA graphs only on Model Runner V2, and is auto-disabled with DP>1
does_not_prove: The page gives no method for choosing the table and no numbers. It does not use acceptance or context length
bearing: supports: adaptive speculation-length control is still a static table. threatens: a plain K-vs-batch idea

title: Adaptive Verification (vLLM docs)
quote: the highest-scoring slots are admitted until a global budget is spent.
proves: vLLM can score each (request, position) draft slot by survival probability and admit slots up to a per-step token budget. The budget comes from a startup cost model of step cost per shape. It is off by default, needs a confidence head, and has no LoRA, PP or enforce-eager support
does_not_prove: The cost model is profiled at startup on a synthetic 8192-token KV context. It does not track live memory pressure, preemption, or KV occupancy
bearing: threatens: a verification-budget scheduling candidate. Budget-aware verification already exists upstream

title: Per-Request Acceptance Metrics (vLLM docs)
quote: This lets a client compute the mean acceptance length and the accepted-draft-length distribution for an individual request.
proves: vLLM exposes per-request acceptance (histogram of accepted drafts per step, plus optional per-step arrays) for single-sequence requests
does_not_prove: The metrics are client-facing. Nothing feeds them back into scheduling, admission or preemption decisions
bearing: supports: an acceptance-aware scheduler can get its per-request signal from existing metrics

title: [RFC]: Automate Speculative Decoding #4565
quote: Paradoxically, under conditions of high request rates or low speculation accuracy, latency may actually increase.
proves: The vLLM roadmap had three milestones: disable SD, then dynamic proposal length, then runtime-only information with no pre-profiling
does_not_prove: Opened May 2024. The milestone 3 goal (no pre-profiled parameters) is still unmet in 2026 (see E2, E6-E8)
bearing: supports: runtime-adaptive speculation as a long-standing open problem

title: [Performance]: Dynamic speculative decoding causes catastrophic aggregate-throughput collapse under concurrency at the batch-size threshold #49548
quote: 8 concurrent 180-token requests dropped from **~232 tok/s aggregate** (static `num_speculative_tokens: 2`) to **24–157 tok/s**
proves: Switching K by batch size near the threshold made throughput collapse (MTP k=2, GB10). A later comment shows the same with DSpark on the V2 runner with full graphs: at concurrency 5, 128 vs 410 tok/s and 423 vs 121 ms/step

title: [Perf] DSD arms pay a large baseline tax vs no-spec under production defaults #49986
quote: At ctx=400, the DSD-mode arms are 20-31% slower than no-spec.
proves: At c=256 on an H100 with Gemma-4-31B, every arm with a speculative_config lost to no-spec at short context (static K=3: -21% at ctx 400). Static K=3 beat no-spec only at ctx 4000 (+10%). Part of the cause is the PIECEWISE CUDA-graph override
does_not_prove: One model and GPU. The K=0 tier still carries a loaded drafter and its KV. The memory share of the tax is not separated out
bearing: supports: the cost of keeping spec enabled at K=0 (drafter KV, graphs) is a real resource question

title: [RFC]: Context-length-aware speculative token scheduling #48627
quote: The batch-only rule "speculation stops paying at high batch" is a short-context artifact, not a general property.
proves: On Gemma-4-31B MTP on an H100, the best-K gain fell from 1.79x at concurrency 30 to 1.00x at 128 for short context. The author proposes keying K on (batch, context)
does_not_prove: The author retracted the long-context gain ratios as warm-up biased (correction dated 2026-08-31). Only the short-context crossover stands
bearing: supports: the crossover depends on context length and KV state, not batch alone. Methodology traps are documented

title: [Feature]: Restore length-based speculation skip or per-request speculative decoding control in V1 #52258
quote: long-document summarization (20K–73K Chinese meeting transcripts) collapses to 5–8% acceptance, making speculation net-negative
proves: On real mixed traffic (EAGLE-3/DFlash), short prompts get 1.6-1.8x but long prompts get 5-8% acceptance. V1 lost V0's per-length skip, and no per-request off switch exists
does_not_prove: This is a user report from one deployment with no controlled study

title: [Bug]: why does enabling MTP speculative decoding actually reduce the prefix cache hit rate? #38182
quote: Prefix cache hit rate: around 71%
proves: On Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with 5500-token fixed prefixes, the prefix-cache hit rate fell from about 92% to about 71% when MTP k=1 was enabled (EAGLE last-block drop on a hybrid model with large blocks)

title: [Misc] Warn when EAGLE/MTP speculation costs a large prefix-cache hit #51769
quote: the one-block drop costs **thousands of tokens per request** instead of a nominal 16.
proves: The EAGLE last-block drop is needed for correctness. On hybrid Mamba/GDN models the enlarged attention block makes it a large, silent hit-rate drop that has been reported repeatedly (#38182, #47194, #43559, #50188)
does_not_prove: The PR only adds a warning. It does not change behavior
bearing: context for E12-E14

title: [RFC]: Lookahead-aware prefix-cache hashing for EAGLE-style draft models #50438
quote: It does not prove equality of `x4`, even though `x4` is part of the draft input that produces the final cache entry at that boundary.
proves: The RFC explains precisely why draft KV at a block boundary depends on the next token: the EAGLE/MTP input shift
does_not_prove: It covers local prefix cache keys only. It does not address preemption or swap of draft state
bearing: threatens: a candidate built on draft-KV prefix-reuse correctness, which is now well understood

title: [Core][Spec Decode] Add lookahead-aware prefix cache hashing for EAGLE-style draft models #50897
quote: Greedy output cannot reveal a wrong draft KV (the target verifies every draft), so the check compares the KV itself.
proves: Putting the lookahead token into the block hash raised hit rate from 72.7% to 85.0% and throughput from 9.09 to 12.43 req/s (+37%) on Qwen3.6-27B MTP k=4, GB200, with unchanged acceptance. A stale-draft-KV negative control gave max abs diff 7.55-14.53, against 0.09-0.29 for correct reuse. It also covers the Offloading, Nixl and Mooncake connectors
does_not_prove: The PR is open and was split (E14). Multi-module MTP keeps the drop

title: [Core][Spec Decode] Lookahead block hashes for EAGLE prefix caching #61589
quote: EAGLE-family drafters write the draft KV at a block's last position from the token after the block, so `main` drops the last matched block on every hit.
proves: Part 1 of #50897, opened 2026-10-14. It covers local prefix cache only. KV-connector support is a stacked part 2. 1,184 CPU unit tests passed
does_not_prove: The GPU benchmarks have not been re-run on the split. It is unmerged as of 2026-10-20
bearing: threatens: the same as E13. This is active work in the last week

title: [Core][Eagle] Fix prefix cache efficiency in prefill phase #44986
quote: Short input (e.g., 2000 tokens, prefix repeat rate 80%，block_size=1536): prefix cache completely failed
proves: With block_size 1536 (hybrid), EAGLE's drop made prefix caching fail fully for short prompts. The PR proposes skipping the drop in prefill
does_not_prove: Results are only in an attached docx. The PR is open, and its reasoning conflicts with E12's (draft KV is written during prefill too)
bearing: context: several competing fixes, so correctness is subtle

title: [Bug]: DFlash2 speculative decoding acceptance permanently collapses to 0% right after prefix cache hit rate goes positive #58894
quote: the drafter keeps proposing tokens every step, but literally none are ever accepted again, for the remainder of the server's uptime.
proves: When the drafter's KV group is not identified, a prefix hit leaves draft state wrong. Acceptance went from 36.9% to 0.0% and stayed there while drafting continued (Qwen3.5 hybrid GDN + DFlash2, Orin)
does_not_prove: Single report on edge hardware with a likely config root cause (no eagle group flagged)

title: [RFC]: Suffix decoding on GPU (suffix_gpu) compatible with async scheduling #51788
quote: the CPU suffix tree needs the committed host token ids each step, and under async scheduling the scheduler runs one step ahead of the worker
proves: In-tree suffix decoding forces async scheduling off. The RFC proposes a GPU-resident suffix index with a cross-request global index (at most 532 MB VRAM in the largest config tested)
does_not_prove: It is an RFC with an external package and is unmerged. The suffix-tree memory budget and eviction policy are left as knobs
bearing: supports: suffix tree and n-gram pool as a managed memory tier (GPU or CPU)

title: [RFC]: Preemption victim-selection extension point (least-computed-first) #54644
quote: Both ignore how much work a request has already done
proves: V1 preemption is recompute-only. The recompute tax reaches about 79% in a forced sweep and 10-23% in realistic online serving. The RFC proposes an lcf victim policy and a pluggable select_victim over read-only features
does_not_prove: The proposed RunningView features (computed, cached, arrival, priority, scheduled) contain no spec state: no acceptance rate, draft KV size or lookahead
bearing: supports: spec-aware preemption victim choice is a gap (the preemption lens)

title: [RFC]: Disaggregated Speculative Decoding with Standalone Parallel Draft Model #42109
quote: a 1B–8B draft can add 10–30% to per-step latency on the target GPUs
proves: Their internal POC moves the drafter to separate GPUs (N:M verify:draft servers, a speculation cache with geometric fan-out, dedicated KV blocks per verify server). It reports about 1.4x TPOT against co-located spec decode at the same GPU budget
does_not_prove: Internal POC, not upstream. It says nothing on draft-server failure, migration, or draft KV consistency when a verify server preempts
