title: [RFC]: Dynamic Speculation Length (DSL) with Confidence-Threshold Early Exit #36657
quote: the exit condition uses the batch-mean confidence, not the minimum
proves: It proposed a per-step draft early exit on batch-mean confidence. The output stays zero-padded to full K so that scheduler and KV see a fixed shape
does_not_prove: Closed. The fixed shape means KV lookahead stays reserved for max K even on early exit
bearing: context: dynamic K does not shrink reserved spec KV

title: [Bug] NGRAM speculative decoding corrupts radix-cached KV with the overlap scheduler when requests end on a stop token #44997 (SGLang)
quote: Greedy speculative decoding should be lossless, so this is silent corruption.
proves: A trailing NGRAM verify step for a finishing request likely writes KV into or over radix-cached prefixes under the overlap scheduler. On 0.5.22, 3/192 greedy outputs were wrong. It was found with exact-answer synthetic-weight probes
does_not_prove: The mechanism is probable, not proven. EOS endings were not measured

title: Speculative Decoding (SGLang docs)
quote: The overlap scheduler currently only supports `--speculative-eagle-topk 1`

quote: Captured hidden states can be large.

title: Speculative Decoding (TensorRT-LLM docs)

title: Speculative Decoding (llama.cpp docs)
quote: Currently, a single hash pool is shared across all server slots, so different requests can benefit from each other.

title: vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/adaptive_verification.py (main @9d4192a)
quote: draft_budget = int(np.argmax(num_tokens_to_estimated_accepted_tokens / costs))
proves: Adaptive verification already conditions on co-scheduled prefill: verify cost is read from the profiled curve starting at num_non_draft_tokens_total (prefill chunks plus one token per decode), and the draft budget maximizes accepted tokens per ms. The prefill chunk size itself is fixed by the scheduler beforehand.
does_not_prove: Objective has no TTFT term and does not shrink prefill chunks; does not move budget from prefill to verify or back.
bearing: C4: narrows the gap to 'add a TTFT term / let the chunk size move', a one-line objective change (simplicity attack).

title: Optimization and Tuning (vLLM docs, latest)
quote: It batches all pending decode requests before scheduling any prefill operations.
proves: With chunked prefill (default in V1), decodes, which include spec tokens, are scheduled first and prefills get what remains of max_num_batched_tokens; smaller budgets (e.g. 2048) favor ITL, larger favor TTFT; >8192 recommended for throughput.
does_not_prove: Page does not mention speculative tokens; no numbers on how much budget verification takes.
bearing: C4 scale attack: at budgets of 8192+, batch 64 x K=3 verification (about 256 tokens) is a few percent of the budget, so the competition is small except at small budgets.

title: An Interpretable Latency Model for Speculative Decoding in LLM Serving
quote: decompose per-request demand into load-independent and load-dependent components for prefill, drafting, and verification
proves: May 2026 model of SD serving latency splits demand into prefill, drafting and verification, and studies how draft length and acceptance shape latency across load.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not mention chunked prefill or TTFT; not a scheduler.
bearing: C4 adjacent: an analytic model that already covers the prefill/verify split, lowering the novelty of a characterization study.

title: MineDraft: A Framework for Batch Parallel Speculative Decoding
proves: Search snippet only: with chunked prefill enabled the batch manager may receive fewer requests in the first SD step, causing draft/target batch imbalance.
does_not_prove: Not opened.
bearing: C4 adjacent, minor.

title: Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context (Table 10 window sweep)
quote: shrinking to 1K is too tight for retrieval and loses acceptance
proves: Window sweep at 1M ctx, d=7: Qwen3.5-35B native AL 4.49 vs W=960 3.79, W=1984 4.74, W=4032 4.74, W=8128 4.16; Qwen3.5-122B native 5.57 vs 4.38/4.20/4.74/4.66; Nemotron-3-120B 3.75 vs 3.64/2.89/3.59/2.89. ~4K draft window (+64 sink) is within -15%..+6% of full-context draft AL; 1K loses ~20% on retrieval.
does_not_prove: MTP heads on hybrid GDN/Mamba targets only (recurrent path carries long range); window always holds correctly built draft KV, never a reset or hole; non-monotonic sweep on one RULER task; no EAGLE or DFlash.
bearing: Kills 'how much draft context is needed' for MTP: ~4K suffices. Narrows C3 to drafters without a recurrent target anchor.

title: H-Spec: Parallel Speculative Decoding Without a Drafter-Side KV Cache (full text)
quote: The attention module consumes target KVs in place.
proves: Block drafter whose attention reads the target's KV in place and whose Mamba modules start from projected last-token target hidden state; no drafter-owned KV, so there is no draft state to keep, move, or rebuild. DFlash baseline MAL 2.47-2.86 (Llama3.1-8B, Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B); H-Spec +5.0-13.3% MAL over best baseline.
does_not_prove: Does not mention preemption, PD, migration, or offload; existing deployed drafters (EAGLE-3, DFlash, most MTP) still own KV.
bearing: Design trend that makes C3 moot for new drafters; threatens C3's longevity.

title: LongSpec: Long-Context Lossless Speculative Decoding with Efficient Drafting and Verification
quote: the window size, which we set to 512
proves: Long-context drafter with 512-token sliding-window self-attention plus cross-attention to the target's KV cache, so draft-owned state is bounded by 512 tokens regardless of context; contrasts with EAGLE whose draft KV grows linearly with context.
does_not_prove: No ablation of window size vs acceptance in fetched text; no serving events (preemption, PD).
bearing: Prior art for 'draft only needs a short window plus target KV'; shrinks C3 novelty.

title: TriForce: Lossless Acceleration of Long Sequence Generation with Hierarchical Speculative Decoding (full text)
quote: its budget is set to 1K
proves: Tiny draft (Llama-68M) runs with a 1K StreamingLLM cache at 122K prompts; naive-policy acceptance 0.27-0.46 depending on temperature; retrieval-cache draft acceptance rises with budget up to 4K then plateaus (Fig. 6a, qualitative).
does_not_prove: Window always well-formed; separate small model, not EAGLE/MTP; no event-driven loss of draft state; plateau numbers not tabulated.
bearing: Supports 'bounded draft window is enough'; precedent for C3's drop-to-window policy.

title: EAGLE 3 / EAGLE 3.1 speculative decoding (AMD ATOM docs)
quote: under long contexts or out-of-distribution prompts, the drafter's attention shifts away from the sink token
proves: EAGLE-3 drafter acceptance collapses at long context as its attention drifts from the sink token; EAGLE 3.1 reports up to 2x acceptance length on long-context production workloads.
does_not_prove: No acceptance-vs-context-length numbers; says nothing about losing or truncating draft KV.
bearing: Signals EAGLE drafters are sensitive to what is in their KV (sink); supports keeping EAGLE in C3's survivor.

title: [Fix] disaggregation: Preserve EAGLE/MTP draft KV during CPU retraction (SGLang PR 44899), PR body GPU section
quote: Read-only observers add CPU copies/synchronization, so no throughput claim is made.
proves: GLM-5.3 MXFP4 on MI350X, two 128k-token prompts, real retraction: draft KV and DSA index snapshots byte-identical after restore on 4/4 ranks over 131063 positions. The authors state missing draft history 'can reduce speculative acceptance' but do not measure it.
does_not_prove: No acceptance-loss number, no cost of the CPU copy of draft KV, no comparison with drop or recompute; open PR with failing CI.
bearing: Confirms engines default to 'preserve' without measuring; leaves cost/benefit open.

title: Preserve full DFlash draft KV during PD CPU retraction (SGLang PR 39749), GPU check
quote: main 98.5% accuracy / average accept length 5.02
proves: Kimi K3 PD 1P1D on 8xB300, DFlash block 8, ~2,950 forced decode retractions on 200 GSM8K questions: accept length 5.02 when draft KV is overwritten by other requests vs 5.29 with draft KV preserved (+5%).
does_not_prove: One run per build; the 5.29 build bundles five PRs; GSM8K short prompts; corrupted (not cleanly dropped) draft KV; no cost of the preservation itself.
bearing: Strongest kill evidence for DFlash: even garbage draft KV costs only ~5% acceptance.

title: [Performance]: DSD K=0 draft-state sync forward costs 4-11% in a K=0 workload; resume impact differs sharply between MTP and EAGLE3 (vLLM issue 53420)
quote: acceptance collapses to ~zero on K>0 resume and does not recover
proves: Skipping draft KV sync for ~950 steps then resuming: Qwen3.6-35B 1-layer MTP keeps 0.985x acceptance at K=2 and 0.84-0.88x at K=8; Llama-3.1-8B EAGLE3 drops to ~0 and never recovers. Keeping the drafter synced costs 4.1-11.3% step time (MTP) and ~7% (EAGLE3).
does_not_prove: Two checkpoints, proxy acceptance metric, single boots; the unsynced positions are stale slots, not a masked clean truncation; short contexts; no catch-up rebuild implemented.
bearing: First measured acceptance-after-draft-state-loss curve: MTP benign, EAGLE3 catastrophic. Kills C3 hypothesis as stated (EAGLE recovers fast).

title: [Core][Spec Decode] Opt-in skip of the K=0 draft sync forward (MTP + DFlash, default off) (vLLM PR 53426)
quote: 14.6% lower, but with no EAGLE-style collapse
proves: DFlash2 on Qwen3.8-27B after unsynced K=0 phases: same-request resume accepts ~3.0 tokens/step; new requests after two K=0 phases 2.87 vs 3.36 static reference (-14.6%). Option refuses EAGLE-family as measured-unsafe; catch-up rebuild named as the correct general fix but not built.
does_not_prove: Single checkpoint per drafter; no rebuild or windowed-rebuild arm; no long-context case.
bearing: Narrows C3 to EAGLE-family rebuild; confirms MTP/DFlash tolerate draft-state holes.

title: [Core][PD] Role-aware optimizations for Spec decoding (vLLM PR 45280), review thread
quote: we still need to prefill the drafter kv cache
proves: Maintainers agree the prefill instance must run the drafter prefill so draft KV for all drafter layers is transferred to decode; discussion is about skipping draft sampling, not about whether transfer beats recompute on D.
does_not_prove: No numbers on drafter prefill time, draft KV bytes, or transfer time; open with merge conflicts.
bearing: Shows vLLM chose 'transfer' for PD by default without a cost study; C3 PD arm unmeasured but low-stakes.

title: [Bug]: Gemma 4 MTP + NIXL PD disaggregation - draft model KV not transferred (vLLM issue 54926), impact section
quote: effectively eliminating any MTP throughput benefit in PD mode
proves: Reporter claims decode pod re-runs 15k+ prompt tokens through draft heads per request at ISL=15k; no comments, no measurement.
does_not_prove: No TTFT, throughput, or acceptance numbers; vLLM's Gemma4 proposer docs (H12) say the assistant's attention layers share the target's KV, so the claimed lost draft KV may not exist on current main.
bearing: Weakens L104 as evidence of a costly recompute; the PD recompute-vs-transfer cost remains unmeasured.

title: vllm.v1.spec_decode.gemma4 proposer API docs
quote: all its attention layers share KV cache with the target model via cross-model KV sharing
proves: Gemma 4 assistant drafter maps each draft decoder layer to the last non-KV-shared target layer of the same attention type; it reads target KV and owns no separate attention KV.
does_not_prove: Docs page; does not discuss PD transfer groups; older versions may differ.
bearing: Second deployed drafter family (after H-Spec/LongSpec designs) where draft state is not separate, making C3 moot.

title: [RFC]: Deprecate kv_both for NIXLConnector and Enforce Explicit P/D Roles (vLLM issue 43807)
quote: P can auto-adjust its speculator config (e.g. set num_speculative_tokens = 1) and skip sampling since it never uses draft tokens
proves: Phase 2 of the PD role RFC treats drafter prefill on P plus transfer as the intended PD design for spec decode.
does_not_prove: No cost data; closed RFC; does not consider recompute on D or dropping draft KV.
bearing: Engine direction = transfer; no measurement exists to challenge or confirm it.

title: DFlash: Block Diffusion for Flash Speculative Decoding (implementation details)
quote: The projected features are stored in the draft model's KV cache and reused across drafting iterations
proves: DFlash drafter has 5 layers (8 for Qwen3 Coder); fused target hidden features are injected into K/V of every draft layer and stored in draft KV. Rebuilding it requires target hidden features for every position, which only a target forward produces.
does_not_prove: No cost of injection relative to target prefill; no truncation study.
bearing: Recompute of DFlash/EAGLE draft KV needs target hidden states, so 'recompute' is cheap only when the target is recomputed too (vLLM preemption), not when target KV survives (swap, offload, PD).

title: RLHFSpec: Breaking the Efficiency Bottleneck in RLHF Training via Adaptive Drafting (migration section)
quote: transfer the KVCache of previous tokens in parallel with the draft generation
proves: Sample migration triggered by a throughput-imbalance reallocator with cooldown; transfers both draft-model and target KV in two stages; prefers migrating short, low-acceptance samples; 5-sample case raised 2,127 to 2,531 tok/s; all overheads combined <3.87%.
does_not_prove: Never compares transfer against recompute or drop of draft KV; RLHF rollout, separate small draft model.
bearing: Kills C6 as a standalone: draft-KV migration is solved by overlapping transfer; leaves only the transfer-vs-drop comparison (C3).

title: NebulaSD: Many-for-Many Speculative Decoding
quote: maintains host-resident KV states for both the draft and target models throughout the lifetime of each active request
proves: Pools draft and target workers, moving each request's draft and target KV between workers via a host-resident KV store with incremental suffix writeback; 50.4% over physically disaggregated and 72.6% over co-located (4 GPUs). Transfers overlapped: 1 GiB D2H slowed draft 2.05% with a separate migration process.
does_not_prove: No transfer-vs-recompute comparison and no acceptance effect; separate draft model.
bearing: Further prior art for moving draft state across workers (C6); treats transfer as the obvious choice.

title: MorphCloud-LLM: Elastic Spot-Instance-Aware LLM Serving with Transparent Preemption Recovery and Speculative Decoding Continuity
proves: Search snippet only: checkpoints KV for spot preemption and keeps draft-model generation going on fallback nodes; cache restoration dominates recovery.
does_not_prove: Fetch returned HTTP 403; content not verified.
bearing: Possible prior art for draft continuity under preemption; check before claiming novelty.

title: [V1][Bug][Spec Decode]: Overhead of SD with PC is 30-40% higher than baseline (vLLM issue 19996)
quote: It seems that overhead of eagle on ttft is 30-40%
proves: H100 Llama-3.1-8B MTBench batch 4: TTFT 14.55 ms baseline vs 18.77 ms EAGLE (1.29x), 14.26 vs 18.56 on repeat; reporter attributes it to scheduler/sampler overhead, not drafter compute.
does_not_prove: Short prompts, old vLLM 0.9.1; does not isolate drafter prefill FLOPs; closed.
bearing: Drafter prefill cost is small in FLOPs (EAGLE 1 layer); fixed overheads dominate, so 'recompute is cheap' holds whenever target hidden states exist.

title: SuffixDecoding: Extreme Speculative Decoding for Emerging AI Applications (Sec. 4.4 ablations, App. B)
quote: the acceptance rate does not change much even when the suffix tree size varies across almost two orders of magnitude
proves: Authors already ablate (a) global-only vs per-request-only vs both on AgenticSQL ('the global tree outperforms the per-request tree on all tasks except for Combine') and (b) tree size 256 to 10,000 output examples: speedup rises with size while acceptance rate is nearly flat. App. B proposes LRU eviction ('incorporate cache eviction (e.g. LRU)') but evaluates no eviction policy; claims ~31 days of tokens fit per A100 host (144 GB CPU RAM).
does_not_prove: No eviction-policy comparison, no Belady/oracle gap, no persistence/warm-start study; size sweep is on offline output examples, not on live multi-agent interleaved traces; global-vs-local split is per task in a figure, not per accepted token on SWE traces.
bearing: C5: Narrows. Kills the 'does global matter' half on AgenticSQL (global wins) and shows acceptance flat vs size, which shrinks the room for a better eviction policy; policy/oracle gap and persistence stay open.

title: OmniDraft: A Cross-vocabulary, Online Adaptive Drafter for On-device Speculative Decoding (App. D.5, Table 14)
quote: LFU plateaus at an earlier stage, with performance matching the full cache even with a quarter of the size.
proves: Published eviction-policy ablation for an online n-gram draft cache: on MBPP+HumanEval, acceptance 0.219 no cache, 0.254 LRU vs 0.259 LFU at 1/4 size, 0.261 vs 0.263 at 1/2, 0.267 full; speedup 1.29x to 1.33-1.36x. Policy gap is about 0.005 acceptance.
does_not_prove: On-device single-user n-gram cache, not a cross-request global suffix tree on agentic traces; no oracle policy; small benchmarks.
bearing: C5: Threatens novelty of 'compare eviction policies for a draft cache' and suggests the policy gap is tiny; does not cover suffix trees or multi-tenant agent traffic.

title: ArcticInference suffix_decoding/cache.py (SuffixDecodingCache)
quote: Evict the first eligible request. Should be FIFO order in Python 3.7+ since dict preserves insertion order.
proves: Eviction is whole-request FIFO keyed on max_cached_requests (negative = unbounded, 0 = no global cache); speculate() queries the per-request tree and the global tree separately and keeps the draft with the higher score, so the source of each draft is recoverable with a one-line change.
does_not_prove: No reuse-aware policy, no byte-based cap, no persistence/serialization API seen; does not say how often global drafts win in practice.
bearing: C5: Confirms FIFO-only baseline and that per-source attribution is cheap to instrument; supports the simulation plan.

title: ArcticInference suffix_decoding/simulator.py
venue: GitHub snowflakedb/ArcticInference (main; last change 2025-10-13 per commit history)
quote: help="Evict a fraction of the cached sequences before running requests"
proves: An offline acceptance simulator already ships with knobs --max-cached-requests, --evict-fraction, --evict-strategy {random, oldest, newest}, --use-cached-prompt; it replays ground-truth responses with greedy tree verification and logs match_len, accepted tokens, spec/update ms per step.
does_not_prove: Eviction is a one-shot fraction removed after warm-up, not online policy under a cap; no LRU/LFU/oracle; eval requests run sequentially (no interleaving); does not log global-vs-local source. No published results from it found.
bearing: C5: Narrows. The cheapest decisive test is mostly a few edits to an existing tool, so the contribution must be the findings (oracle gap, interleaved agent traces), not the harness.

title: vLLM docs: Speculative Decoding (suffix decoding options)
quote: Maximum number of requests cached in the global suffix tree. Set `0` to disable the global cache.
proves: vLLM exposes suffix_decoding_max_cached_requests (default 10000, 10x lower than Arctic's 100000) and suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth (default 24).
does_not_prove: Page says nothing about eviction policy or persistence across restarts.
bearing: C5: Confirms capacity is a user knob with no guidance; supports the capacity-curve question.

title: Suffix decoding drafts almost nothing under PP: the per-step decode rotation destroys each request's suffix tree (vllm-rbln issue 1084)
quote: a rejoining request evicts its own cached response first
proves: In vLLM's suffix proposer, a request absent from the input batch is treated as finished and its per-request tree is destroyed; under PP=4 rotation acceptance fell from 97.4% (concurrency 1) to 4.5% (concurrency 4); max_cached_requests=10000 vs 0 made no difference (51 vs 52 accepted). A patch restored 79.1% acceptance and 58.73 to 99.68 tok/s. Closed not planned (stale) 2026-10-18.
does_not_prove: Vendor fork under PP; upstream vLLM behaviour under ordinary preemption not tested here; single reporter.
bearing: C5 (and C7): Supports that per-request tree loss on preemption/rotation is real and large, which is a stronger and narrower gap than global eviction policy.

title: Beat the long tail: Distribution-Aware Speculative Decoding for RL Training
quote: moderate windows (16 or 32) strike a better balance between acceptance and latency
proves: Suffix-tree drafter for RL rollouts uses a sliding window of recent trajectories with per-problem trees and down-weighting of older matches; window ablation (16, 32, all): larger windows raise acceptance but window_all has the highest latency.
does_not_prove: Window is in RL iterations, tied to policy drift; no memory cap, no eviction-policy comparison, no serving/multi-tenant setting.
bearing: C5: Prior art for recency-based retention of a suffix draft cache; narrows novelty of 'recency vs capacity' claims.

title: SAM Decoding: Speculative Decoding via Suffix Automaton
quote: we constructed a static suffix automaton based on the Vicuna-7B generation results
proves: Static (offline corpus) plus dynamic (per-generation) suffix automata; ablation on Spec-Bench: removing the static module drops speedup 1.84x to 1.64x, removing the dynamic module drops it to 1.33x; static automaton supplies drafts in 2.45% of cases.
does_not_prove: No corpus size, memory, or eviction/update policy for the static store; Spec-Bench, not agentic traffic.
bearing: C5: Supports the hypothesis that the per-request (dynamic) store does most of the work on general traffic; does not settle agentic traffic.

title: nebius/SWE-agent-trajectories
quote: The dataset is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license.
proves: 80,036 SWE-agent trajectories, 1.11 GB, CC BY 4.0; fields include instance_id, model_name (e.g. swe-agent-llama-70b), trajectory (full reasoning/action/observation log), generated_patch.
does_not_prove: Trajectory is a single string log, not token-level outputs from one tokenizer; no timestamps, so arrival interleaving must be synthesized; outputs are from older open models.
bearing: C5: Makes trace-replay simulation feasible on CPU with a permissive license.

title: nvidia/SWE-Hero-openhands-trajectories
quote: This dataset is governed by the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0).
proves: 34,269 OpenHands trajectories over 11,766 issues, ~2.4 GB parquet, generated by Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct; trajectory is a role-tagged message list (assistant actions, tool observations), so assistant outputs can be tokenized and replayed per turn.
does_not_prove: No timing; one generator model, so cross-model/tenant diversity is absent; many trajectories per issue may inflate global-cache hits versus real traffic.
bearing: C5: Best-fit public multi-turn agent trace for global-vs-local suffix attribution; caveat on duplicated issues.

title: nvidia/Nemotron-SWE-v1
quote: The trajectories were synthesized using state-of-the-art Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct.
proves: ~59k agent trajectories (card), ~11 GB, CC BY 4.0 with some BSD-3-Clause subsets; messages list plus execute_bash tool schema.
does_not_prove: Row counts on the card conflict (24,875 vs 34,772 vs 59k); fetch could not confirm tool outputs are included.
bearing: C5: Second permissive agent trace source; same single-generator caveat.

title: A First Look at Bugs in LLM Inference Engines
quote: Testing LLM inference engines requires diverse oracles beyond mere crash detection.
proves: 929 bugs from 5 engines (incl. vLLM, TensorRT-LLM); 28 root causes; no speculative-decoding, preemption, or scheduling category; closest: Concurrency Issue 39 (~4.2%), Incorrect Cache Management 11 (~1.2%), Inconsistent Output 17 (~1.8%); notes outputs vary 'even after disabling all randomness settings'.
does_not_prove: Only first 100k of 142k characters read; mined bugs predate the 2026 spec+async+hybrid cluster; no test harness built.
bearing: C7: Supports novelty: the main empirical bug study has no spec-decode or preemption class and calls for better oracles.

title: Continuous Discovery of Vulnerabilities in LLM Serving Systems with Fuzzing (GRIEF)
quote: lets new variants (e.g. EAGLE-3, Medusa) and entirely new serving modes reuse
proves: Greybox fuzzer for vLLM and SGLang using timed multi-request traces, KV-utilization/scheduler-pressure feedback, and replay-based logprob confirmation of output divergence; 15 potential vulnerabilities, 10 confirmed, 2 CVEs; 7 state-corruption bugs (cross-request KV reuse). Preemption occurs only incidentally; speculative decoding is named as future adapter work and no spec bugs are reported.
does_not_prove: Does not inject preemption/offload at chosen step boundaries, does not check acceptance equivalence, does not cover spec decode.
bearing: C7: Biggest novelty threat. Narrows C7 to 'spec-aware state-event injection with acceptance oracle'; a GRIEF spec adapter could pre-empt it quickly.

title: vLLM docs: Batch Invariance
quote: Batch invariance is currently in beta.
proves: Batch-invariant mode exists in vLLM (beta; NVIDIA CC>=8.0, AMD Instinct, Intel XPU with Triton), with TP limits and a performance cost.
does_not_prove: Page does not mention speculative decoding, preemption, or prefix caching, so whether greedy spec+preemption runs are bitwise comparable under it is undocumented. Not available on Metal.
bearing: C7: Neutral; the oracle precondition (bitwise-equal greedy runs) is not documented for spec decode.

title: SGLang docs: Deterministic Inference
quote: Radix Cache Consistency mode: test radix cache determinism (cached vs uncached prefill)
proves: SGLang deterministic mode supports CUDA graph, chunked prefill, radix cache (FA3, Triton; not FlashInfer) and temp>0; its built-in tests check same prompt across batch sizes, prefix lengths, and cached vs uncached prefill.
does_not_prove: No mention of speculative decoding, EAGLE, preemption, or retraction; its tests do not move state mid-request.
bearing: C7: Supports gap: SGLang's determinism checks stop at prefill caching; no retract/resume or spec coverage.

title: Towards Deterministic Inference in SGLang and Reproducible RL Training (LMSYS blog)
proves: Future-work list covers faster kernels, MoE, on-policy RL, radix cache, TP, FlexAttention; speculative decoding and preemption/retraction are not mentioned at all.
does_not_prove: Absence claim only; quote not captured verbatim by fetch tool.
bearing: C7: Weak support that deterministic-mode roadmaps do not target spec or retraction.

title: Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference (Thinking Machines Lab)
quote: all of our 1000 completions are identical
proves: Batch-invariant kernels made 1000 temp-0 Qwen3-235B completions identical (80 unique without); attention must be invariant to chunked prefill and prefix caching splits.
does_not_prove: No mention of speculative decoding or preemption; does not address verify-shape changes (1+k tokens) or draft-model state.
bearing: C7: Supplies the oracle precondition in principle; leaves spec/preemption untreated.

title: vLLM tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py
quote: Test consistency and acceptance rates with some different combos of preemption, executor, async scheduling, prefill chunking, spec decoding model length.
proves: vLLM CI already runs a differential test: EAGLE-3 (k=2) and ngram_gpu (k=3) runs with forced preemption (num_gpu_blocks_override=33, ~34 concurrent prompts), async scheduling, uni/mp executor and chunking are compared to a non-spec baseline on token outputs, logprobs, and acceptance rate (within 5%, 10% on ROCm), under FP32 matmul and FlexAttention.
does_not_prove: Preemption is induced by pressure, not injected at chosen step boundaries; covers only EAGLE-3 and ngram_gpu (no suffix, MTP, DFlash, draft_model, hybrid GDN/Mamba, KV offload, PD handoff); acceptance tolerance of 5% would hide small silent acceptance loss.
bearing: C7: Narrows hard. The 'compare against uninterrupted run, outputs + acceptance' oracle exists in vLLM CI; the remaining gap is step-targeted injection and coverage of hybrid/offload/PD/suffix paths.

title: [Test] Rework e2e async scheduling tests (vLLM PR 28744)
quote: Various improvements, more selective combos of features.
proves: The preemption x spec x async consistency suite dates from Nov 2025 (merged 2025-11-15).
does_not_prove: PR text does not list the combos; content inferred from the test file (I18).
bearing: C7: Shows the differential suite is ~1 year old, not new.

title: [BugFix] Fix num_output_placeholders preemption underflow (vLLM PR 48245)
quote: Reproduces deterministically with PP + async scheduling under KV pressure
proves: Stale in-flight spec output returning after KV-pressure preemption underflowed counters and crashed EngineCore, most visible with spec decode/PP at high concurrency; found on GLM-5.2-FP8 TP4/PP2 with MTP at concurrency 32-128, not by the CI suite; regression tests added (test_kv_pressure_preemption_with_inflight_output, num_spec in {0,3}).
does_not_prove: A crash, not silent divergence; regression tests are scheduler-level unit tests for this one path.
bearing: C7: Supports that the existing differential suite missed a spec+preemption bug found only at scale; also shows fixes add point regressions rather than a systematic harness.

title: LLM-42: Enabling Determinism in LLM Inference with Verified Speculation
quote: When the verifier detects a mismatch, LLM-42 rolls the sequence back to the last matching token.
proves: Determinism via decode-verify-rollback with the same model; recomputation overhead 6.81% at window 32, 46.41% at 256.
does_not_prove: Does not address preemption or separate-drafter speculative decoding; it is a determinism mechanism, not a test method.
bearing: C7: Tangential; shows rollback-based determinism is studied, but not equivalence of spec state across preemption.

title: [Spec Decode] Lazily catch up draft KV after zero-K steps (#734)
quote: record the earliest missing draft-KV position during K=0 without running the draft model, then lazily ingest the complete missing range before the next K>0 proposal
proves: Merged 2026-09-15 (by LxYuan0420, author POWEHI2023). Implements lazy draft-KV catch-up after K=0 steps; lazy path only with prefix caching off ("enable_prefix_caching=True keeps the eager" path); median wall 0.8610 s eager vs 0.7754 s lazy, -9.94%, on Qwen3-0.6B dynamic K, three alternating pairs; proposal hashes, target outputs and acceptance counts identical across six processes (18/18 accepted).

title: Utility-Driven Speculative Decoding for Mixture-of-Experts (Cascade)

quote: We present, Cascade, a utility-driven speculation framework to dynamically disable speculation if it is detrimental.
